directions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given below each sentence. Select the best answer to complete the sentence. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

questions.stem: The quarterly sales figures will be reviewed ____ the board meeting on Friday afternoon.
questions.explanation: 'During' shows the review happens within the time span of the meeting; the others cannot introduce an event like this.

questions.stem: The new scheduling software has significantly improved the ____ of our customer service team.
questions.explanation: A singular noun is needed after 'the' and before 'of', so 'efficiency' is correct.

questions.stem: Neither the department manager nor her assistants ____ available to comment on the merger.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'assistants', which is plural, so 'are'.

questions.stem: Because the shipment was delayed, the company had to ____ its customers about the new delivery date.
questions.explanation: Only 'inform' takes a person as its direct object ('inform its customers about'); the others require a different structure.

questions.stem: The consultant ____ recommendations saved us thousands of dollars is presenting again today.
questions.explanation: The possessive relative pronoun 'whose' is needed before the noun 'recommendations'.

questions.stem: This year's turnout was far ____ than last year's, exceeding all of the organizers' expectations.
questions.explanation: The word 'than' signals a comparison between two years, so the comparative 'larger' is required.

questions.stem: ____ the proposal was submitted on time, the committee decided to postpone its final decision.
questions.explanation: The contrast between an on-time submission and a postponement calls for the concession word 'Although'.

questions.stem: The technicians ____ the equipment three times this week, but it keeps malfunctioning.
questions.explanation: A repeated action within the unfinished period 'this week' takes the present perfect 'have repaired'.

questions.stem: Despite the tight deadline, the contract negotiations proceeded ____ from start to finish.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'proceeded', so 'smoothly' is correct.

questions.stem: Please submit your expense reports ____ the end of the month to ensure timely reimbursement.
questions.explanation: 'By' marks a deadline meaning 'no later than', whereas 'until' would imply a continuous action up to that point.

questions.stem: The board members praised the marketing team for ____ innovative and cost-effective campaign.
questions.explanation: A possessive adjective is needed before the noun 'campaign', so 'their' is correct.

questions.stem: The keynote address at the annual conference will be ____ by the company's chief executive.
questions.explanation: The passive structure 'will be ____' requires the past participle 'delivered'.

questions.stem: The proposed merger will ____ nearly every department, so managers should prepare their teams.
questions.explanation: The verb 'affect' means 'to influence'; 'effect' as a verb means 'to bring about', which does not fit here.

questions.stem: The finance office is responsible for ____ the annual budget and reviewing all departmental spending.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'for', a gerund is required, so 'preparing' is correct.

questions.stem: Each of the shortlisted applicants ____ required to complete a written assessment before the interview.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Each' is singular, so the singular verb 'is' is correct.

questions.stem: The store will remain open ____ the renovations on the ground floor are completely finished.
questions.explanation: 'Until' marks the point up to which the store stays open; 'during' and 'despite' cannot introduce a clause here.

questions.stem: The assembly instructions were so ____ that none of the new employees could follow them.
questions.explanation: The '-ing' adjective 'confusing' describes something that causes confusion, which fits the instructions.

questions.stem: By the time the external auditors arrived, the accountant ____ all of the financial records.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had organized' shows the action was completed before another past event.

questions.stem: The company specializes ____ manufacturing environmentally friendly packaging for the food industry.
questions.explanation: The verb 'specialize' is followed by the preposition 'in'.

questions.stem: Of all the candidates interviewed this week, she was clearly the ____ qualified for the position.
questions.explanation: Comparing one person against an entire group requires the superlative, so 'the most qualified'.

questions.stem: All managers are expected to ____ to the company's revised data-protection guidelines.
questions.explanation: 'Adhere' correctly pairs with 'to'; 'comply' takes 'with', and 'observe' and 'follow' take a direct object without 'to'.

questions.stem: The interns completed the entire inventory project by ____ without any supervision.
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun 'themselves' is used in the phrase 'by themselves', meaning on their own.

questions.stem: The regional office is seeking an experienced ____ to lead its expanding finance department.
questions.explanation: A noun naming a person is needed after 'an experienced', so 'supervisor' is correct.

questions.stem: ____ you have any questions about the new policy, please contact the human resources department.
questions.explanation: A conditional meaning is required, so 'If' introduces the clause correctly.

questions.stem: Ticket prices for the trade show range ____ fifty to two hundred dollars depending on the package.
questions.explanation: The pattern 'range from...to...' requires 'from'; 'between' would need 'and' instead of 'to'.

questions.stem: We will notify you by email as soon as your order ____ from our distribution center.
questions.explanation: In a time clause introduced by 'as soon as', the present simple 'ships' expresses future meaning.

questions.stem: The mobile application is ____ designed for users with limited technical experience.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the participle 'designed', so 'specifically' is correct.

questions.stem: The manager decided to ____ the meeting until all of the department heads could attend.
questions.explanation: 'Postpone...until' means to delay to a later time, which fits waiting for the department heads.

questions.stem: ____ of the two proposals offers a decisive advantage, so the team will continue developing both.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' with a singular verb fits the logic that no single proposal stands out, so both are kept.

questions.stem: When ____ properly, the machine can operate for years with very little additional maintenance.
questions.explanation: The reduced passive clause 'When (it is) maintained properly' requires the past participle 'maintained'.

Reviewed by Kenji T.  ★★★★☆
Stayed at the Lakeside Inn for three nights.

The Lakeside Inn exceeded my expectations for a mid-range hotel. My room was spotless, the bed was comfortable, and the desk was large enough to spread out my work — a detail many hotels overlook. The complimentary breakfast was fresh and included plenty of options, though it ended a bit early at 9 A.M., which was inconvenient on the morning of a late meeting.

The staff deserve special praise. When my presentation remote stopped working, the front desk found a spare within minutes. The only real drawback was the noise from the highway, which I noticed at night. If you're a light sleeper, ask for a room facing the lake.

Overall, I would happily stay here again and recommend it to other business travelers.

Bowl & Grain Opens Fourth Location Downtown

Bowl & Grain, the fast-casual chain known for its build-your-own grain bowls, opened its fourth city location on Prescott Street last week. The new branch is the company's largest yet and the first to stay open until 10 P.M. on weekends.

To celebrate the opening, Bowl & Grain is offering a free drink with any bowl through the end of the month. The company also announced a new mobile app that lets customers order ahead and earn a free bowl for every ten purchased.

"We built the app because our regulars told us they wanted to skip the lunchtime line," said marketing director Nina Fales. Customer feedback, she added, continues to shape the menu; a new roasted-vegetable bowl was added this spring after repeated requests.

TOEIC Mock Tests — Reading Practice Test 2（toeicmocktests.com，官方 2026 格式）

directions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given below each sentence. Select the best answer to complete the sentence. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

questions.stem: All visitors must sign in at the front desk ____ entering the laboratory.
questions.explanation: 'Before' + gerund shows the sign-in happens prior to entering; the others do not fit this time relationship.

questions.stem: The marketing team worked ____ to meet the tight product-launch deadline.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'worked', so 'tirelessly' is correct.

questions.stem: Ms. Ford, ____ presentation impressed the investors, has been promoted to director.
questions.explanation: The possessive relative pronoun 'whose' is needed before the noun 'presentation'.

questions.stem: The company's profits have grown ____ over the past three years.
questions.explanation: An adverb is required to modify the verb 'have grown', so 'steadily' is correct.

questions.stem: Neither the supervisor nor the technicians ____ satisfied with the revised schedule.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'technicians', which is plural, so 'are'.

questions.stem: Employees are encouraged to ____ any concerns directly with their supervisors.
questions.explanation: 'Raise' takes a direct object ('raise any concerns'); 'rise' and 'arise' are intransitive.

questions.stem: The new safety regulations will take effect ____ the first of January.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'on' is used with a specific date, so 'on the first of January'.

questions.stem: By the time the guests arrived, the caterers ____ all of the food.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had prepared' shows the action was completed before another past event.

questions.stem: The final report must be submitted ____ Friday, or the project may be delayed.
questions.explanation: 'By' marks a deadline meaning 'no later than', whereas 'until' would imply continuing up to that point.

questions.stem: The training session was so ____ that several attendees asked for a follow-up.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed after 'so', and 'informative' describes the session.

questions.stem: Each of the branch offices ____ its own annual sales target to meet.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Each' is singular, so the singular verb 'has' is correct.

questions.stem: The agency is looking for a talented ____ to manage its social media accounts.
questions.explanation: A noun naming a person is needed after 'a talented', so 'coordinator' is correct.

questions.stem: The proposal was rejected ____ it exceeded the approved budget by a wide margin.
questions.explanation: 'Because' introduces the reason the proposal was rejected.

questions.stem: Customers who spend over one hundred dollars ____ a complimentary gift at checkout.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'Customers' takes the plural verb 'receive'.

questions.stem: The new intern adapted to the role far more ____ than anyone had expected.
questions.explanation: With 'more...than', the base adverb 'quickly' is required to form the comparison.

questions.stem: The equipment ____ in the factory is inspected every six months for safety.
questions.explanation: The reduced passive clause 'the equipment (that is) used' requires the past participle 'used'.

questions.stem: Please make sure that all contracts are ____ signed before they are filed.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the participle 'signed', so 'properly' is correct.

questions.stem: The success of the campaign depends ____ how well we understand our customers.
questions.explanation: The verb 'depend' is followed by the preposition 'on'.

questions.stem: ____ the weather was poor, the outdoor concert still attracted a large crowd.
questions.explanation: The contrast between poor weather and a large turnout calls for the concession word 'Although'.

questions.stem: This printer model is far more reliable than ____ the office used last year.
questions.explanation: 'The one' refers back to a single printer model, matching 'This printer model'.

questions.stem: The auditor asked all staff to ____ with the new reporting procedures.
questions.explanation: 'Comply' pairs with 'with'; 'adhere' would take 'to', and 'observe' and 'obey' take a direct object.

questions.stem: The projector will be ____ by a technician before the presentation begins.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'set up' completes the passive structure 'will be set up'.

questions.stem: Ticket sales this month were higher than in ____ month this year.
questions.explanation: 'Any other' correctly compares this month against every remaining month.

questions.stem: The company reported a significant ____ in online orders during the holiday season.
questions.explanation: A singular noun is needed after 'a significant', so 'increase' is correct.

questions.stem: The new software allows managers ____ employee schedules from their phones.
questions.explanation: The pattern 'allow + object + to-infinitive' requires 'to adjust'.

questions.stem: Visitors are not permitted to enter the warehouse floor ____ a safety helmet.
questions.explanation: 'Without' + noun means lacking a helmet; 'unless' would need a clause, not a noun.

questions.stem: The two departments must work together ____ to complete the merger smoothly.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'work together', so 'closely' is correct.

questions.stem: ____ arriving at the airport, please proceed directly to the check-in counter.
questions.explanation: 'Upon arriving' means immediately after arriving, which fits the instruction.

questions.stem: Of all the applicants, Ms. Reyes had the ____ experience in project management.
questions.explanation: Comparing one person against the whole group requires the superlative, so 'the most'.

questions.stem: The shipment will be delivered ____ it clears the customs inspection.
questions.explanation: 'As soon as' introduces the time at which the delivery will happen.

Chapters & Co. Opens Flagship Store With Café

Chapters & Co., the independent bookseller, opened its largest store yet on Halden Square last weekend. The new location is the first to include a full café and the first to stay open until 9 P.M. on weeknights.

TOEIC Mock Tests — Reading Practice Test 3（toeicmocktests.com，官方 2026 格式）

directions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given below each sentence. Select the best answer to complete the sentence. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

questions.stem: The manager reviewed the proposal carefully ____ approving the additional funding.
questions.explanation: 'Before' + gerund shows the review happens prior to the approval.

questions.stem: The customer service team responded ____ to every complaint it received.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'responded', so 'promptly' is correct.

questions.stem: Mr. Ito, ____ team won the innovation award, will lead the new division.
questions.explanation: The possessive relative pronoun 'whose' is needed before the noun 'team'.

questions.stem: Sales in the online store have risen ____ since the website was redesigned.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'have risen', so 'sharply' is correct.

questions.stem: Neither the director nor the board members ____ aware of the delay until yesterday.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'board members', which is plural, so 'are'.

questions.stem: The new privacy policy will ____ all employees, so please read it carefully.
questions.explanation: The verb 'affect' means 'to influence'; 'effect' as a noun and the others do not fit here.

questions.stem: The store will reopen ____ Monday, once the holiday weekend is over.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'on' is used with a day, so 'on Monday'.

questions.stem: By the time the manager called, the team ____ the presentation.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had finished' shows the action was completed before another past event.

questions.stem: Applications must be received ____ the end of the month to be considered.
questions.explanation: 'By' marks the deadline meaning 'no later than'.

questions.stem: The guest lecture was so ____ that no one wanted it to end.
questions.explanation: The '-ing' adjective 'interesting' describes something that causes interest, which fits the lecture.

questions.stem: Each of the regional offices ____ submitted its annual report on time.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Each' is singular, so the singular verb 'has' is correct.

questions.stem: The firm hired an experienced ____ to oversee the construction project.
questions.explanation: A noun naming a person is needed after 'an experienced', so 'manager' is correct.

questions.stem: The outdoor concert was cancelled ____ a severe storm over the region.
questions.explanation: 'Because of' introduces a noun phrase giving the reason for the cancellation.

questions.stem: Employees who complete the survey ____ entered into a prize draw.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'Employees' takes the plural passive verb 'are entered'.

questions.stem: The second design was received far more ____ than the first by the review panel.
questions.explanation: With 'more...than', the base adverb 'favorably' is required to modify 'was received'.

questions.stem: The documents ____ during the meeting will be circulated to all staff tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The reduced passive clause 'the documents (that were) discussed' requires the past participle 'discussed'.

questions.stem: Please ensure the machine is ____ shut down at the end of each working day.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'shut down', so 'completely' is correct.

questions.stem: The launch date depends ____ the results of the final round of tests.
questions.explanation: The verb 'depend' is followed by the preposition 'on'.

questions.stem: ____ the report was thorough, it arrived a full week after the deadline.
questions.explanation: The contrast between a thorough report and its lateness calls for the concession word 'Although'.

questions.stem: This supplier's service is far more dependable than ____ we used before.
questions.explanation: 'The one' refers back to a single supplier, matching 'this supplier'.

questions.stem: All staff must ____ with the updated fire-safety rules without exception.
questions.explanation: 'Comply' pairs with 'with'; 'adhere' would take 'to', and the others take a direct object.

questions.stem: The booth will be ____ by the marketing team before the trade show opens.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'set up' completes the passive structure 'will be set up'.

questions.stem: Our flagship store earns more revenue than ____ branch in the country.
questions.explanation: 'Any other' correctly compares the flagship store against every remaining branch.

questions.stem: There has been a noticeable ____ in customer inquiries since the campaign began.
questions.explanation: A singular noun is needed after 'a noticeable', so 'rise' is correct.

questions.stem: The new app allows users ____ their orders in real time from any device.
questions.explanation: The pattern 'allow + object + to-infinitive' requires 'to track'.

questions.stem: No one may access the server room ____ proper authorization from IT.
questions.explanation: 'Without' + noun means lacking authorization; 'unless' would need a clause.

questions.stem: The two teams collaborated ____ to finish the project ahead of schedule.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'collaborated', so 'closely' is correct.

questions.stem: ____ receiving your confirmation, we will ship your order the same day.
questions.explanation: 'Upon receiving' means immediately after receiving, which fits the promise.

questions.stem: Of all the proposals submitted, hers was the ____ practical and well researched.
questions.explanation: Comparing one proposal against the whole group requires the superlative, so 'the most'.

questions.stem: We will contact you ____ a decision has been made about your application.
questions.explanation: 'As soon as' introduces the time at which the contact will happen.

Reviewed by Dominic R.  ★★★★☆
Aeris X2 Noise-Canceling Headphones

I bought the Aeris X2 mainly for long train commutes, and they have transformed my daily ride. The noise cancellation is genuinely impressive; the rumble of the carriage all but disappears once I switch it on. The padding is soft, and I can wear them for two hours without discomfort.

Battery life is the standout feature — I charge them once a week at most. My only real complaint is the carrying case, which is bulky and doesn't fit easily into a laptop bag. I also wish the controls were a bit easier to find by touch.

Still, for the price, these are excellent, and I'd recommend them to anyone who commutes.

FreshCart Launches Same-Day Delivery in Elmwood

FreshCart, the online grocery service, expanded to the Elmwood district this month, becoming the first grocer in the area to offer same-day delivery on orders placed before noon. The company sources much of its produce from farms within the region.

To mark the launch, FreshCart is waiving delivery fees on first orders through the end of the month. It also introduced an updated app that lets customers save favorite items and earn a $5 credit for every five completed orders.

"Shoppers told us the number-one thing they wanted was groceries arriving the same day, not two days later," said regional manager Dahlia Ferris. "So that became our priority for Elmwood."

★★★☆☆  Reviewed by Colin M.

I signed up for FreshCart mostly because of the same-day delivery — a real help on busy weekdays. My first order arrived within a few hours, the produce was fresh, and I liked not paying a delivery fee.

My frustration was the app. I tried to save a list of favorite items so I could reorder quickly, but the list kept disappearing, and my order credit never showed up in my account. I placed the order through the website in the end. Customer service was polite and looked into it. I'll keep using FreshCart for the speed, but the app needs fixing.

TOEIC Mock Tests — Reading Practice Test 5（toeicmocktests.com，官方 2026 格式）

directions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given below each sentence. Select the best answer to complete the sentence. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

questions.stem: Staff should back up their files ____ they leave the office for the holiday weekend.
questions.explanation: 'Before' introduces the clause showing the backup happens prior to leaving; the others cannot fit here.

questions.stem: The keynote speaker addressed the audience ____ despite the technical difficulties on stage.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'addressed', so 'confidently' is correct.

questions.stem: Mr. Salazar, ____ proposal secured the largest client this year, will lead the account.
questions.explanation: The possessive relative pronoun 'whose' is needed before the noun 'proposal'.

questions.stem: The commute downtown is ____ longer during the winter months than in the summer.
questions.explanation: 'Much' correctly intensifies the comparative adjective 'longer'.

questions.stem: Neither the caterer nor the florists ____ confirmed their arrival time for the gala.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'florists', which is plural, so 'have'.

questions.stem: The board agreed to ____ the launch date until the software had been fully tested.
questions.explanation: 'Postpone...until' means to delay to a later time, which fits waiting for the testing to finish.

questions.stem: The company picnic has been scheduled ____ the second Saturday of September.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'on' is used with a specific day, so 'on the second Saturday'.

questions.stem: By the time the reporters arrived, the spokesperson ____ the official statement.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had released' shows the action was completed before another past event.

questions.stem: All feedback forms should be returned ____ the close of business on Friday.
questions.explanation: 'By' marks a deadline meaning 'no later than', whereas 'until' would imply continuing up to that point.

questions.stem: The negotiations were so ____ that the two sides needed a full week to reach an agreement.
questions.explanation: The '-ed' adjective 'complicated' describes the nature of the negotiations.

questions.stem: Each of the finalists ____ a portfolio of previous work to the selection panel.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Each' is singular, so the singular verb 'presents' is correct.

questions.stem: The startup is recruiting a talented ____ to design its mobile banking interface.
questions.explanation: A noun naming a person is needed after 'a talented', so 'developer' is correct.

questions.stem: ____ the instructions were clearly written, several customers still assembled the shelf incorrectly.
questions.explanation: The contrast between clear instructions and errors calls for the concession word 'Although'.

questions.stem: Guests who book a suite ____ offered complimentary access to the rooftop lounge.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'Guests' takes the plural passive verb 'are offered'.

questions.stem: The redesigned checkout page loads far more ____ than the previous version on mobile devices.
questions.explanation: With 'more...than', the base adverb 'quickly' is required to modify 'loads'.

questions.stem: The recommendations ____ in the audit report will be discussed at next week's meeting.
questions.explanation: The reduced passive clause 'the recommendations (that were) made' requires the past participle 'made'.

questions.stem: Please ensure the confidential documents are ____ stored in the locked cabinet.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the participle 'stored', so 'securely' is correct.

questions.stem: The success of the fundraiser depends largely ____ the generosity of our regular donors.
questions.explanation: The verb 'depend' is followed by the preposition 'on'.

questions.stem: The manager praised the team ____ completing the migration without any downtime.
questions.explanation: The pattern 'praise someone for something' requires 'for'.

questions.stem: This year's conference venue is far more spacious than ____ we booked in the past.
questions.explanation: 'The one' refers back to a single venue, matching 'this year's conference venue'.

questions.stem: Suppliers must ____ with the company's ethical sourcing requirements to remain approved.
questions.explanation: 'Comply' pairs with 'with'; 'adhere' would take 'to', and the others take a direct object.

questions.stem: The temporary partitions will be ____ once the open-plan office is ready for use.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'taken down' completes the passive structure 'will be taken down'.

questions.stem: Our downtown café attracts more foot traffic than ____ location in the city.
questions.explanation: 'Any other' correctly compares this café against every remaining location.

questions.stem: The report highlighted a steady ____ in energy consumption across all three facilities.
questions.explanation: A singular noun is needed after 'a steady', so 'decline' is correct.

questions.stem: The new dashboard permits managers ____ performance data from a single screen.
questions.explanation: The pattern 'permit + object + to-infinitive' requires 'to monitor'.

questions.stem: Contractors cannot begin work on site ____ a valid permit from the city council.
questions.explanation: 'Without' + noun means lacking a permit; 'unless' would require a clause, not a noun.

questions.stem: The research and marketing divisions worked ____ to bring the product to market on time.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'worked', so 'closely' is correct.

questions.stem: ____ signing the lease, tenants should read every clause of the agreement carefully.
questions.explanation: 'Before signing' correctly places the careful reading prior to signing the lease.

questions.stem: Of all the routes considered, this one is the ____ cost-effective for regular deliveries.
questions.explanation: Comparing one route against the whole set requires the superlative, so 'the most'.

questions.stem: We will process your refund ____ the returned item has been inspected by our warehouse.
questions.explanation: 'Once' introduces the time at which the refund will be processed.

CityWheels Car Sharing Expands to Maple Ridge

CityWheels, the hourly car-sharing service, added the Maple Ridge neighborhood to its network this week, its first location with vehicles parked directly on residential streets rather than in central lots. Members can now find a car within a short walk of most homes in the area.

To celebrate, CityWheels is waiving the annual membership fee for anyone who joins before the end of the month. The company also released an updated app that shows real-time vehicle locations and awards a free hour of driving for every ten trips completed.

"Our members told us the biggest hurdle was walking twenty minutes to reach a car," said operations lead Farid Naderi. "Putting vehicles on neighborhood streets solves that."

TOEIC Mock Tests — Reading Practice Test 6（toeicmocktests.com，官方 2026 格式）

directions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given below each sentence. Select the best answer to complete the sentence. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

questions.stem: Employees are asked to switch off their monitors ____ leaving the building each evening.
questions.explanation: 'Upon leaving' means at the moment of leaving, which fits the instruction; the others cannot introduce this action.

questions.stem: The technician explained the safety procedure ____ so that everyone could follow along.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'explained', so 'clearly' is correct.

questions.stem: Ms. Ahmadi, ____ department exceeded its targets, was invited to present at headquarters.
questions.explanation: The possessive relative pronoun 'whose' is needed before the noun 'department'.

questions.stem: The updated model is considerably ____ to operate than the one it replaced.
questions.explanation: The comparison with 'than' requires the comparative form 'easier'.

questions.stem: Neither the editor nor the writers ____ satisfied with the proposed cover design.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'writers', which is plural, so 'were'.

questions.stem: The airline offered passengers a voucher to ____ for the lengthy delay.
questions.explanation: 'Compensate for' means to make up for something negative such as a delay; the others do not fit this pattern.

questions.stem: The grand opening of the flagship store is planned ____ the middle of October.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'in' is used with a month or period, so 'in the middle of October'.

questions.stem: By the time the shift ended, the volunteers ____ more than three hundred meals.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had served' shows the action was completed before another past event.

questions.stem: Registrations for the workshop must be completed ____ the end of the week.
questions.explanation: 'By' marks a deadline meaning 'no later than', whereas 'until' would imply continuing up to that point.

questions.stem: The lecture on market trends was so ____ that the audience took extensive notes.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed after 'so', and 'informative' describes the lecture.

questions.stem: Each of the departments ____ responsible for preparing its own quarterly forecast.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Each' is singular, so the singular verb 'is' is correct.

questions.stem: The airline is hiring a qualified ____ to manage its regional flight schedules.
questions.explanation: A noun naming a person is needed after 'a qualified', so 'coordinator' is correct.

questions.stem: The delivery was refused ____ the packaging showed clear signs of damage.
questions.explanation: 'Because' introduces the reason the delivery was refused.

questions.stem: Members who renew early ____ granted access to the exclusive online library.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'Members' takes the plural passive verb 'are granted'.

questions.stem: The upgraded engine runs far more ____ than the standard model under heavy loads.
questions.explanation: With 'more...than', the base adverb 'efficiently' is required to modify 'runs'.

questions.stem: The comments ____ during the review will be incorporated into the next draft.
questions.explanation: The reduced passive clause 'the comments (that were) collected' requires the past participle 'collected'.

questions.stem: Please make sure the invoices are ____ labeled before they are sent to accounting.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the participle 'labeled', so 'accurately' is correct.

questions.stem: The final approval of the design rests ____ the senior architect on the project.
questions.explanation: 'Rest with someone' means to be that person's responsibility, so 'with' is correct.

questions.stem: ____ the store had advertised the sale for weeks, very few customers showed up.
questions.explanation: The contrast between weeks of advertising and low turnout calls for the concession word 'Although'.

questions.stem: The current accounting system is much slower than ____ the firm installed years ago.
questions.explanation: 'The one' refers back to a single system, matching 'the current accounting system'.

questions.stem: Every contractor is required to ____ to the confidentiality terms of the agreement.
questions.explanation: 'Adhere' pairs with 'to'; 'comply' would take 'with', and the others take a direct object without 'to'.

questions.stem: The trade-show booth will be ____ by the crew the night before the doors open.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'set up' completes the passive structure 'will be set up'.

questions.stem: Our online store generates more revenue than ____ channel the company operates.
questions.explanation: 'Any other' correctly compares the online store against every remaining channel.

questions.stem: The survey revealed a marked ____ in customer satisfaction after the redesign.
questions.explanation: A singular noun is needed after 'a marked', so 'improvement' is correct.

questions.stem: The new plan enables employees ____ their vacation days entirely online.
questions.explanation: The pattern 'enable + object + to-infinitive' requires 'to request'.

questions.stem: Visitors may not photograph the exhibits ____ prior consent from the gallery.
questions.explanation: 'Without' + noun means lacking consent; 'unless' would require a clause, not a noun.

questions.stem: The sales and support teams collaborated ____ to resolve the client's complaint.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'collaborated', so 'swiftly' is correct.

questions.stem: ____ submitting the application, please double-check that all fields are complete.
questions.explanation: 'Before submitting' correctly places the check prior to submitting the application.

questions.stem: Among the three suppliers evaluated, this one offered the ____ favorable payment terms.
questions.explanation: Comparing one supplier against the whole group requires the superlative, so 'the most'.

questions.stem: We will dispatch your order ____ the payment has cleared our system.
questions.explanation: 'As soon as' introduces the time at which the order will be dispatched.

GearUp Cycles Opens Downtown Service Hub

GearUp Cycles, the bicycle service chain, opened its newest hub on Weaver Street this week — its largest yet and the first to stay open until 8 P.M. on weekdays for after-work repairs. The hub offers same-day tune-ups, a wide parts inventory, and a comfortable waiting lounge with free coffee.

To celebrate, GearUp is offering a free safety check with any repair through the end of the month. The chain also launched a mobile app that lets customers book repair slots in advance and earn a free tune-up for every six services.

"Riders told us they couldn't get to a shop before it closed after work," said service manager Delia Frost. "The later hours and the app are our answer to that."

I brought my commuter bike to the new Weaver Street hub on a weekday evening, mainly because it stays open late — a real lifesaver since I finish work at six. The tune-up was quick and well done, and the free coffee in the lounge was a nice touch.

My frustration was the app. I tried to book my slot in advance, but it kept freezing at the confirmation screen, and my service count never updated toward the free tune-up. options.B: She invited him to a grand-opening event.
options.C: She fixed the app problem and added a free tune-up credit to his account.
options.D: She asked him to visit another hub.

questions.explanation: Marcus's app froze and lost his service count; Ms. Frost says the problem was fixed and she added a free tune-up credit.

questions.stem: In the email, the word 'recording' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: The feature 'recording correctly' means logging the service count correctly, so 'logging' is closest.

TOEIC Mock Tests — Reading Practice Test 7（toeicmocktests.com，官方 2026 格式）

directions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given below each sentence. Select the best answer to complete the sentence. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

questions.stem: Your travel coordinator will send you a detailed ____ listing all flight times and hotel addresses.
questions.explanation: An itinerary is a travel plan that lists flights and hotels, so (C) is correct. (A) 'inventory' is a list of stock, (B) 'agenda' is a list of topics for a meeting, and (D) 'invoice' is a bill.

questions.stem: Ms. Oyelaran ____ the hospital's volunteer program since it was founded in 2019.
questions.explanation: 'Since it was founded' describes a period that continues up to now, which requires the present perfect (A) 'has coordinated'. (B) 'coordinates' and (C) 'coordinated' cannot be used with 'since' in this way, and (D) 'will coordinate' is future.

questions.stem: Employees who have worked at Kestrel Logistics for at least six months are ____ for the tuition assistance program.
questions.explanation: 'Eligible for' means meeting the conditions to take part, so (D) is correct. (A) 'capable' is followed by 'of', (C) 'entitled' is followed by 'to', and (B) 'considerable' means large in amount.

questions.stem: To ____ the printer's deadline, the design team divided the catalog pages among three editors.
questions.explanation: 'Meet a deadline' is the standard collocation, so (B) is correct. (A) 'obey' is used with rules or orders, (C) 'attend' is used with events, and (D) 'comply' needs 'with'.

questions.stem: The owner of the food truck has applied for a ____ to serve customers along the riverside promenade on weekends.
questions.explanation: After the article 'a', a noun is needed, and (A) 'permit' is an official document that allows an activity. (B) 'permitted' is a verb form, and (C) 'permissive' and (D) 'permissible' are adjectives with no noun to describe.

questions.stem: ____ the client approves the revised layout by this afternoon, the brochures can still be printed before the trade fair.
questions.explanation: (C) 'Provided that' means 'on the condition that': if approval comes today, printing is still possible. (A) 'Unless' reverses this logic, and (B) 'Although' and (D) 'Whereas' express contrast, which does not fit.

questions.stem: Every runner who completes the half-marathon will receive a ____ T-shirt and a finisher's medal.
questions.explanation: 'Complimentary' means given free of charge, which suits a gift for every finisher, so (D) is correct. (A) 'complicated' means difficult, (B) 'competent' means skilled, and (C) 'compulsory' means required.

questions.stem: The storage facility, ____ is located just off the ring road, offers climate-controlled units for artwork and wine.
questions.explanation: A relative pronoun for a thing that is also the subject of 'is located' is needed, so (B) 'which' is correct. (A) 'who' refers to people, (C) 'where' cannot act as a subject, and (D) 'what' cannot refer back to a noun.

questions.stem: Because the delay was caused by the bank's own error, it has agreed to ____ the late-payment fee.
questions.explanation: To 'waive' a fee is to cancel it, which is a fair response to the bank's own mistake, so (D) is correct. (A) 'impose' and (B) 'collect' would mean charging the fee, and (C) 'accrue' means to build up over time.

questions.stem: The clinic's new poster campaign aims to ____ awareness of the importance of regular eye examinations.
questions.explanation: 'Raise awareness' is a fixed collocation, so (A) is correct. (B) 'rise' and (C) 'arise' are intransitive verbs that cannot take an object, and (D) 'gather' is not used with 'awareness'.

questions.stem: Hotel guests have found the new self-service check-in kiosks surprisingly ____ to use.
questions.explanation: In the pattern 'find + object + adjective', an adjective is needed, so (C) 'intuitive' is correct. (B) 'intuitively' is an adverb (the adverb 'surprisingly' already modifies the adjective), (A) 'intuition' is a noun, and (D) 'intuit' is a verb.

questions.stem: The number of passengers using the airport's express rail link ____ doubled since the fares were reduced.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' is a singular subject, so (B) 'has' is correct, forming the present perfect 'has doubled'. (A) 'have' wrongly agrees with 'passengers', and (C) 'are' and (D) 'were' do not form the needed tense.

questions.stem: The renovated city hall was designed to ____ wheelchair users, with ramps and wide doorways on every floor.
questions.explanation: To 'accommodate' wheelchair users is to provide for their needs, so (A) is correct. (B) 'accompany' means to go with someone, (C) 'acquire' means to obtain, and (D) 'accumulate' means to collect gradually.

questions.stem: Ms. Takahashi prefers to review the supplier contracts ____ rather than assign the task to an assistant.
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun (D) 'herself' shows that Ms. Takahashi does the review personally. (A) 'she' is a subject pronoun, and (B) 'her' and (C) 'hers' cannot be added after a complete clause to give this meaning.

questions.stem: The dates for the regional sales summit are still ____ and may change once the venue is confirmed.
questions.explanation: Dates that 'may change' are not final, so (C) 'tentative' is correct. (A) 'definite' means the opposite, (B) 'punctual' means on time, and (D) 'reluctant' describes people who are unwilling.

questions.stem: The free downtown shuttle bus runs every twenty minutes ____ 7:00 A.M. and 11:00 P.M.
questions.explanation: The pattern 'between ... and ...' marks a period with two end points, so (A) is correct. (B) 'among' is used with groups, and (C) 'within' and (D) 'throughout' are not paired with 'and' in this way.

questions.stem: The research firm will ____ a series of interviews with frequent business travelers to learn how they choose hotels.
questions.explanation: Researchers 'conduct' interviews, meaning they carry them out, so (B) is correct. (A) 'reserve' and (D) 'book' are used for rooms, seats, or tickets, and (C) 'admit' means to let in or to confess.

questions.stem: Pre-orders for the folding electric scooter have already ____ the manufacturer's forecast for the entire year.
questions.explanation: Numbers that go beyond a forecast have 'exceeded' it, so (D) is correct. (A) 'excelled' means performed very well and does not take this object, (B) 'exited' means left, and (C) 'extended' means made longer.

questions.stem: The board is considering ____ a second warehouse closer to the port to reduce delivery times.
questions.explanation: The verb 'consider' is followed by a gerund, so (C) 'leasing' is correct. (B) 'to lease' is a common error after 'consider', and (A) 'lease' and (D) 'leased' cannot follow 'considering'.

questions.stem: The architects' revised floor plan is ____ similar to the version they presented in March.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the adjective 'similar', so (D) 'remarkably' is correct. (B) 'remarkable' is an adjective, (A) 'remark' is a noun or verb, and (C) 'remarked' is a past verb form.

questions.stem: Ms. Kowalczyk accepted the sustainability award ____ the entire logistics department.
questions.explanation: Accepting an award 'on behalf of' a group means doing so as its representative, so (B) is correct. (A) 'in charge of' means managing, (C) 'in favor of' means supporting, and (D) 'regardless of' means without considering.

questions.stem: The winners of this year's young chefs' competition ____ at a ceremony in Lisbon next month.
questions.explanation: The winners do not announce anything; they are announced, so a passive verb is needed, and 'next month' requires the future: (A) 'will be announced'. (B) and (C) are active, and (D) is past.

questions.stem: Audience members are asked to ____ from using their phones while the performance is in progress.
questions.explanation: Only 'refrain' is followed directly by 'from' + -ing with no object, so (C) is correct. (A) 'avoid' takes a gerund without 'from', and (B) 'prevent' and (D) 'prohibit' need an object before 'from'.

questions.stem: The building manager has requested that each tenant ____ the updated fire-safety checklist before Friday.
questions.explanation: After 'request that', the base form of the verb is used for every subject, so (D) 'complete' is correct. (A) 'completes' is a common error here, (B) 'completed' is past tense, and (C) 'completing' is not a finite verb.

questions.stem: ____ at the free lunchtime concerts in Bellmont Square has risen every summer since the series began.
questions.explanation: The number of people who go to an event is its 'attendance', so (A) is correct. (C) 'Attendant' is a person who helps others, (B) 'Attention' means focus, and (D) 'Appearance' refers to being seen or to how something looks.

questions.stem: The new meeting room on the fifth floor holds twice as many people ____ the old one did.
questions.explanation: The structure 'twice as many ... as' requires (C) 'as'. (A) 'than' follows comparative forms such as 'more', and (B) 'so' and (D) 'like' cannot complete this comparison.

questions.stem: Restaurants that ____ an order with Delvaux Produce by 9 P.M. receive their delivery the next morning.
questions.explanation: Customers 'place' an order with a supplier, so (B) is correct. (A) 'fill' an order is what the supplier does, and (C) 'set' and (D) 'hand' are not used with 'order' in this sense.

questions.stem: Before choosing a contractor, the manager of the climbing gym requested a written ____ for resurfacing the entrance ramp.
questions.explanation: A written 'estimate' states the expected cost of work before it begins, so (D) is correct. (A) 'receipt' is given after payment, (B) 'statement' summarizes an account, and (C) 'refund' is money paid back.

questions.stem: If an applicant's forms are incomplete, the registration office will return ____ with a checklist of the missing items.
questions.explanation: An object pronoun is needed after 'return' to replace 'forms', so (B) 'them' is correct. (A) 'they' is a subject pronoun, (C) 'their' must be followed by a noun, and (D) 'themselves' would refer back to the subject.

questions.stem: The east entrance will be ____ closed while the new revolving door is installed.
questions.explanation: The entrance is closed only for as long as the installation takes, so (A) 'temporarily' is correct. (B) 'formerly' and (C) 'previously' refer to the past, and (D) 'eventually' means in the end, which does not match 'while'.

directions: Read the texts that follow. A word, phrase, or sentence is missing in parts of each text. Four answer choices for each question are given below the text. Select the best answer to complete the text. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

To: Tobias Lindqvist <t.lindqvist@quillmail.com>
From: Subscriber Services, Vellacourt Concert Hall
Date: August 14
Subject: Your seats for the new season

Dear Mr. Lindqvist,

Thank you for renewing your subscription for our new concert season, which (1)____ on September 6 with the opening gala. We are writing to let you know about a change to your usual seats in Row F.

The canopy will greatly improve the sound throughout the auditorium, but the equipment needed to complete the work will occupy the first six rows of seating until the end of September. (2)____, your seats for the September concerts have been moved to Row K, directly behind your usual location. (3)____

From October onward, you will return to your regular seats in Row F. If the temporary location is not suitable, please contact us before August 31, and we will issue a full (4)____ for the September concerts.

Sincerely,
Helena Marsh
Subscriber Services

questions.stem: Blank (1)
questions.explanation: The email is dated August 14 and the season opens on September 6, a future date, so (B) 'will begin' is correct. (A) 'began', (C) 'has begun', and (D) 'had begun' all describe the season as having already started.

questions.stem: Blank (2)
questions.explanation: Moving the seats to Row K is a result of the front rows being occupied, so (D) 'Therefore' is correct. (A) 'Even so' and (B) 'In contrast' signal contrast, and (C) 'For instance' introduces an example.

questions.stem: Blank (3)

options.A: Your new seats offer an equally good view of the stage.
options.B: The opening gala will feature a guest conductor from Vienna.
options.C: Tickets for individual concerts went on sale last week.
options.D: We regret that your subscription could not be renewed.

questions.explanation: Right after the seats are moved to Row K, a reassuring comment about the new seats fits naturally, so (A) is correct. (B) and (C) change the topic, and (D) contradicts the opening line, which thanks Mr. Lindqvist for renewing.

questions.stem: Blank (4)
questions.explanation: If the new seats are unsuitable, the hall offers to return the money for those concerts, a full 'refund', so (C) is correct. (A) 'receipt' is proof of payment, (B) 'deposit' is a partial payment made in advance, and (D) 'discount' is a price reduction, which would not be called 'full'.

docs.text:
Bring Your Rooftop to Life with Canopy Hive Partners

Is the roof of your office building an empty, unused space? (1)____ Canopy Hive Partners installs and manages beehives on commercial rooftops throughout the Dunmore region, allowing your company to support local wildlife without doing any of the work.

Our certified beekeepers visit every two weeks during the warmer months to inspect the hives and keep the colonies healthy. (2)____, they give short lunchtime talks so that your employees can learn how bees live and why they matter to local farms and gardens.

Each autumn, the honey from your hives is harvested, (3)____ in jars carrying your company logo, and delivered to your office. Many of our clients give these jars to customers and visitors as gifts.

Installation takes less than a day, and our team handles every safety requirement. To arrange a free rooftop (4)____, call 555-0182 or visit www.canopyhive.com.

questions.stem: Blank (1)

options.A: Most roof repairs are covered by standard building insurance.
options.B: Honey prices have fallen sharply across the region this year.
options.C: It could be home to thousands of honeybees.
options.D: Our beekeepers will train your staff to look after the hives themselves.

questions.explanation: The sentence answers the opening question about an empty roof and leads into the description of the beehive service, so (C) is correct. (A) and (B) are unrelated to the service, and (D) contradicts the promise that the company does all the work.

questions.stem: Blank (2)
questions.explanation: The lunchtime talks are an extra service on top of the hive inspections, so (A) 'In addition' is correct. (B) 'Nevertheless' signals contrast, (C) 'Instead' signals replacement, and (D) 'Otherwise' introduces a different result.

questions.stem: Blank (3)
questions.explanation: The blank is part of a list of passive actions, 'is harvested, ____, and delivered', so the past participle (D) 'packed' keeps the list parallel. (A) 'pack', (B) 'packing', and (C) 'to pack' break the parallel structure.

questions.stem: Blank (4)
questions.explanation: Before hives are installed, the roof must be checked, so a free rooftop 'assessment' (B) is correct. (A) 'admission' means entry, (C) 'attendance' means being present, and (D) 'allowance' is an amount of money given regularly.

questions.stem: Blank (2)
questions.explanation: The sentence offers a second way to power the scanner instead of the battery, so (C) 'Alternatively' is correct. (A) 'Consequently' signals a result, (B) 'For example' introduces an example, and (D) 'Likewise' signals similarity.

questions.stem: Blank (3)
questions.explanation: 'Ideal for' means perfectly suited to, which fits a tool for people who handle a lot of paperwork, so (B) is correct. (A) 'eager' and (C) 'fond' describe people's feelings, and (D) 'capable' is followed by 'of', not 'for'.

questions.stem: Blank (4)

options.A: The scanner was discontinued last year.
options.B: Shipping charges depend on the weight of your order.
options.C: Please bring your receipt when you collect your repaired scanner.
options.D: Orders placed before 2 P.M. are dispatched the same day.

docs.text:
Old Grain Store Reborn as Riverside Food Hall

After sitting empty for almost two decades, the Calder Street Grain Store in Port Ellis reopened last Saturday as a food hall with twenty-six independent vendors. The brick warehouse, built in 1911 to store wheat (1)____ arrived by barge, now houses stalls selling everything from Ethiopian coffee to Korean street food.

The building's new owners, Nora Abernathy and Kofi Mensah, spent three years restoring the structure. (2)____ "We wanted visitors to feel the history of the place the moment they walk in," said Ms. Abernathy.

Opening day drew more than 5,000 people, far more than the owners had expected. (3)____, several vendors sold out of food by mid-afternoon. The owners plan to (4)____ the hall's opening hours on weekends once vendors have hired additional staff.

questions.stem: Blank (1)
questions.explanation: A relative pronoun is needed to refer to 'wheat' and act as the subject of 'arrived', so (D) 'that' is correct. (A) 'what' cannot follow a noun, (B) 'who' refers to people, and (C) 'where' refers to places.

questions.stem: Blank (2)

options.A: Parking near the waterfront is limited on weekends.
options.B: They kept the original iron beams and wooden floors wherever possible.
options.C: Most of the vendors have never run a restaurant before.
options.D: The warehouse is scheduled to be demolished next spring.

questions.explanation: A detail about keeping the original beams and floors describes the restoration and leads into Ms. Abernathy's comment about the building's history, so (B) is correct. (A) and (C) do not connect to her quote, and (D) contradicts the reopening.

questions.stem: Blank (3)
questions.explanation: Vendors selling out early was a consequence of the unexpectedly large crowd, so (C) 'As a result' is correct. (A) 'In contrast' signals contrast, (B) 'Otherwise' introduces an alternative, and (D) 'For instance' introduces an example.

questions.stem: Blank (4)
questions.explanation: To 'extend' opening hours is to make them longer, which suits a popular hall, so (A) is correct. (B) 'explore' means to investigate, (C) 'exceed' means to go beyond a limit, and (D) 'expose' means to uncover.

directions: In this part you will read a selection of texts, such as magazine and newspaper articles, e-mails, and instant messages. Each text or set of texts is followed by several questions. Select the best answer for each question and mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

docs.title: Text-message chain
docs.text:
Ana Ribeiro (3:02 P.M.): Viktor, the labels on the Montrose Foods pallets show the Westport depot code. That order is supposed to go to Eastbrook.
Viktor Sandberg (3:04 P.M.): All of them? The truck for that order arrives at 4:30.
Ana Ribeiro (3:05 P.M.): Twenty-two pallets. And the label printer at my station is jammed, so I can't print new ones here.
Viktor Sandberg (3:06 P.M.): Use the printer in the returns area. I'll send Chidera over to help you relabel them.
Ana Ribeiro (3:08 P.M.): Thanks. Even with two of us, it will take a little over an hour.
Viktor Sandberg (3:09 P.M.): That'll be tight. I'll let the driver know he may have to wait a few minutes.

questions.stem: What problem does Ms. Ribeiro report?

options.A: A truck has arrived earlier than scheduled.
options.B: Some pallets were damaged during loading.
options.C: Some pallets have labels with the wrong destination.
options.D: A client has canceled part of an order.

questions.explanation: Ms. Ribeiro writes that the labels on the Montrose Foods pallets show the Westport depot code although the order should go to Eastbrook, so (C) is correct. The truck is not due until 4:30 (A), and nothing is said about damage (B) or a cancellation (D).

questions.stem: At 3:09 P.M., what does Mr. Sandberg most likely mean when he writes, 'That'll be tight'?

options.A: There will be very little time to spare before the pickup.
options.B: The pallets will be difficult to fit on the truck.
options.C: The returns area does not have enough space.
options.D: The new labels must be attached very firmly.

questions.explanation: Ms. Ribeiro says that relabeling will take a little over an hour, and the truck arrives at 4:30, so Mr. Sandberg means the work will barely be finished in time, which is why he plans to warn the driver (A). He is not talking about space on the truck (B) or in the returns area (C), or about how the labels are attached (D).

docs.title: Notice
docs.text:
CITY OF MERRITON
Planning Department

NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING

The Merriton Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on Tuesday, March 10, at 6:30 P.M. in the Council Chamber of City Hall, 200 Ordway Street. The commission will consider an application from Velmont Distribution to build a storage and distribution center on the vacant lot at the corner of Kilbride Road and Station Lane.

Under the proposal, a new access road would connect the site directly to Route 9 so that delivery trucks would not need to travel through the residential streets east of the lot. The full plans may be viewed at the Planning Department counter on weekdays from 8:30 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. or online at www.merriton.gov/planning.

Residents who are unable to attend the hearing may submit written comments to planning@merriton.gov. Comments must be received by noon on Monday, March 9, to be shared with commission members before the hearing.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the notice?

options.A: To inform the public about a meeting on a building proposal
options.B: To announce the opening of a distribution center
options.C: To request bids for the construction of a road
options.D: To report that the city has sold a vacant lot

questions.explanation: The notice announces a public hearing at which the Planning Commission will consider Velmont Distribution's application to build a facility, so (A) is correct. The center has not been built, so nothing is opening (B), no bids are requested (C), and nothing says the city has sold the lot (D).

questions.stem: What is indicated about Velmont Distribution's plan?

options.A: It has already been approved by the commission.
options.B: It would replace an older building on Station Lane.
options.C: Its details are available only at City Hall.
options.D: It is designed to keep trucks off residential streets.

questions.explanation: The notice explains that a new access road would connect the site to Route 9 so that delivery trucks would not travel through the residential streets east of the lot, so (D) is correct. The hearing has not happened yet, so the plan is not approved (A); the lot is vacant, so no building would be replaced (B); and the plans can also be viewed online (C).

HOTEL SOLENNE
Express Check-Out

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the information?

options.A: To announce a change in check-out time
options.B: To explain a quicker way to check out
options.C: To explain how to arrange a late check-out
options.D: To request feedback about the hotel's staff

questions.explanation: The card explains how guests can leave without waiting in line at the front desk by using the Express Check-Out box, so (B) is correct. The 11:00 A.M. check-out time is stated but not changed (A), late check-out is not discussed (C), and guests are not asked for feedback (D).

questions.stem: What should a guest who needs a printed receipt do?

options.A: Pick it up from the Express Check-Out box
options.B: Ask the concierge on the day of departure
options.C: Call the front desk before leaving the room
options.D: Reply to the e-mail sent by the hotel

questions.explanation: Guests who need a printed receipt are told to dial 0 from the room phone to reach the front desk before they leave, so (C) is correct. The box is only for key cards (A), the concierge looks after luggage (B), and replying to the e-mail is not mentioned (D).

docs.title: Email
docs.text:
To: Siobhan Gallagher, Hotel Marisco
From: Piotr Wierzbicki, Brantwood Furniture Works
Date: April 2
Subject: Order 5521 (bedside tables)

Dear Ms. Gallagher,

I am writing about your order of 140 bedside tables for the guest rooms at the Hotel Marisco. Our supplier of walnut veneer has just informed us that its next shipment will reach our factory two weeks later than planned. As a result, we will not be able to complete the full order by your requested delivery date of May 4.

We can, however, deliver 80 tables on May 4 as scheduled, with the remaining 60 following by May 18. Since I understand that your renovation is proceeding one floor at a time, I hope this arrangement will still suit your timeline. Please let me know by Friday which floors should receive the first delivery so that our warehouse can label the cartons accordingly.

To make up for the inconvenience, there will be no charge for the second delivery. I apologize for this change and thank you for your understanding.

Sincerely,
Piotr Wierzbicki
Customer Accounts

questions.stem: Why did Mr. Wierzbicki send the e-mail?

options.A: To confirm that an order has been canceled
options.B: To request payment for a recent shipment
options.C: To recommend a different type of wood
options.D: To explain that an order will be delivered in two parts

questions.explanation: Mr. Wierzbicki explains that because of a delay in materials, 80 tables will arrive on May 4 and the remaining 60 by May 18, so (D) is correct. The order is not canceled (A), no payment is requested (B), and he does not suggest another kind of wood (C).

questions.stem: What is suggested about the Hotel Marisco?

options.A: It is preparing to open a second location.
options.B: It is being renovated in stages.
options.C: It has bought furniture from Brantwood before.
options.D: It has requested a discount on its order.

questions.explanation: Mr. Wierzbicki notes that the hotel's renovation is proceeding one floor at a time, which suggests the work is being done in stages (B). A second location (A) and earlier purchases (C) are not mentioned, and the free second delivery is Brantwood's own offer, not a discount the hotel requested (D).

questions.stem: What is Ms. Gallagher asked to do?

options.A: Pay a fee for the second delivery
options.B: Choose a different finish for the tables
options.C: Indicate where the first tables should go
options.D: Be present when the cartons are labeled

questions.explanation: Ms. Gallagher is asked to say by Friday which floors should receive the first delivery, so (C) is correct. The second delivery will be free (A), no change of finish is mentioned (B), and Brantwood's warehouse will label the cartons without her (D).

www.lockwellparcel.com/lockers

Lockwell Parcel | Collect at a Locker

Not at home during the day? Have your parcels delivered to one of our 300 self-service lockers in train stations, supermarkets, and community centers across the region. Lockers are open 24 hours a day, so you can pick up your items whenever it suits you.

How It Works
1. When shopping online, choose "Lockwell Locker" as your delivery option and select a location.
2. As soon as your parcel has been placed in a locker, we will send you a six-digit code by text message.
3. Enter the code on the locker's touch screen, and the door will open.

Collection Time
Parcels are held for five days. Any parcel that has not been collected by the end of the fifth day will be returned to the sender, who may charge a fee to send it again. Lockers accept parcels up to 60 centimeters on the longest side and up to 15 kilograms in weight.

For Businesses
Our new Locker Plus plan allows small online sellers to drop off up to 50 outgoing parcels a day at any locker location. Visit our Business page to learn more.

To: All Production Staff, Wardle Glassworks
From: Mattias Ekholm, Plant Manager
Date: August 3
Re: Furnace 2 maintenance week

As announced at last month's staff meeting, Furnace 2 will be shut down from Monday, August 17, to Friday, August 21, so that its worn interior lining can be replaced. During this period, the bottle line that the furnace supplies will not operate.

Employees who normally work on the bottle line will be given other duties that week. Some will assist our contractor, Arkell Refractory Services, with the relining work, while others will join the packing team or complete their annual safety refresher course. Supervisors will post individual assignments on the notice board by August 10.

Please also note that the north gate on Bellfield Road will be closed for the entire week, as the contractor will be using the yard behind it to store equipment and materials. Staff who normally use that gate should enter through the main entrance on Wardle Way instead.

If you have any questions, please speak to your shift supervisor.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
March 18
Contact: Margaux Lefèvre, Communications Director, (555) 0172

Saltmere Hotels to Welcome Guests' Dogs

Saltmere Hotels announced today that, beginning June 1, guests traveling with dogs will be welcome at all fourteen of its properties. — [1] —. The decision follows a survey in which nearly a third of the company's regular guests said they had stayed elsewhere because they could not bring their pets.

Dogs will be allowed only in designated rooms on the first two floors of each hotel, close to the exits. — [2] —. Each of these rooms will be supplied with a dog bed, food and water bowls, and a small welcome package of treats. A cleaning fee of $30 per stay will apply.

Saltmere has also partnered with local dog-walking businesses in every city where it operates, so guests attending meetings or dining out can arrange a walk through the front desk. — [3] —.

"Many of our guests consider their dogs part of the family," said Saltmere chief executive Adebayo Fashola. "We want both of them to feel at home with us." — [4] —. Pet-friendly rooms can be reserved on the Saltmere website or by telephone.

Linmouth to Test On-Demand Minibus Service
By Ifeoma Nwankwo, Staff Writer

Starting July 1, residents of Linmouth's northern neighborhoods will be able to request a ride on a city-run minibus through a smartphone app or by telephone. The six-month trial, approved by the city council on Tuesday, will replace Bus Route 14, which runs once an hour and carries an average of only nine passengers per trip. — [1] —.

Unlike a regular bus, the new service will not follow a fixed route. Instead, riders will be picked up within a short walk of their homes and taken to any destination inside the service zone, which includes the North Linmouth train station, Eastmoor Medical Center, and the Castlegate Shopping Arcade. — [2] —. Fares will be the same as on regular city buses, and monthly passes will be accepted.

"Route 14 was costly to run and inconvenient for many of the people who rely on it," said Thandiwe Dube, the city's director of transportation. — [3] —. "With this approach, we can offer more frequent and flexible service for roughly the same cost."

Five minibuses, each seating twelve passengers, will be leased for the trial. — [4] —. If the results are positive, the council may extend the service to the eastern districts next year.

options.B: A trial of a flexible public transportation service

questions.explanation: The article reports that Linmouth will run a six-month trial of an on-demand minibus service that does not follow a fixed route, so (B) is correct. The train station is only one destination (A), fares will stay the same as on regular buses (C), and Ms. Dube is simply quoted as the city's director of transportation; nothing says she was newly appointed (D).

questions.explanation: The article states that the council may extend the service to the eastern districts next year if the results are positive, so (C) is correct. Operating hours (A) and business owners (B) are not mentioned, and Ms. Dube says the cost will be roughly the same as before (D).

Skerry Line to Add Overnight Freight Sailing

Businesses on Kilbrannan Island will soon have a faster way to get their goods to the mainland. Beginning on Monday, May 4, Skerry Line will operate a freight-only sailing from Kilbrannan to the port of Ardmore every night except Sunday. The ship will leave at 11:30 P.M. and arrive at 4:00 A.M., in time for goods to reach the mainland's early-morning markets and the Ardmore rail freight terminal.

At present, all freight travels on Skerry Line's three daily passenger ferries. During the busy summer months, these ferries are often full, and trucks are sometimes left on the pier to wait for the next sailing.

The freight ship can carry up to 40 trucks and trailers. Businesses that book space on the same night each week for at least three months will receive a 15 percent discount. All bookings must be made at least 48 hours before departure, either online or at the freight office on Kilbrannan Pier.

"Island producers have been asking for a service like this for years," said Skerry Line freight manager Aurelio Batista.

Brackwater District Council
Economic Development Office
45 Guildhall Square, Brackwater

February 2

Dear Business Owner,

We are pleased to announce the return of the Storefront Improvement Grant, which helps small businesses in the Old Market area improve the outside of their premises. Last year, the program funded 32 projects, from new signs to restored windows, and the results can be seen throughout the district.

This year, grants will cover 50 percent of eligible costs, up to a maximum of $4,000 per business. Eligible projects include signs, exterior lighting, awnings, painting, and window or door repairs. Interior work and equipment purchases are not eligible.

To apply, complete the enclosed form and return it with written quotes from two licensed contractors and at least one photograph of your current storefront. Applications must be received by March 15. Because funds are limited, grants will be awarded in the order in which complete applications are received.

If you have any questions, please contact Vikram Sethi at (555) 0127.

Sincerely,
Defne Arslan
Director of Economic Development

docs.title: Email
docs.text:
To: sanitation@haverlytownship.gov
From: Takumi Hayashi
Date: October 15
Subject: Recycling at 52 Orchard Crescent

Hello,

Yesterday I found a notice on my recycling bin explaining that it could not be emptied because the lid was not closed. That was fair. We had just received a delivery of new furniture, and the packaging would not fit inside the bin.

I have since flattened the boxes, but there is still far more cardboard than the bin can hold, so I would like to take it to the recycling center myself. Since I work long hours during the week, the weekend would be best for me. Could you tell me whether I need to bring proof that I live in the township?

Also, one of my neighbors mentioned that collection on our street will move to a different day next year. Is that correct?

Thank you,
Takumi Hayashi

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the schedule?

options.B: To introduce a new recycling center
options.C: To list fees for collecting extra cardboard
options.D: To explain a temporary change to collection days

questions.explanation: The schedule explains that, because of the Harvest Day holiday, collection in every zone will be one day later than usual during the week of October 12, so (D) is correct. The zones themselves are unchanged (A), the recycling center is mentioned only as a drop-off point (B), and dropping off cardboard is free (C).

questions.stem: In which zone does Mr. Hayashi most likely live?
questions.explanation: The notice was left on October 14. Since Monday was October 12, that date was the Wednesday of the holiday week, when collection was for Zone B, whose regular day is Tuesday. So (B) is correct. Zone C (C) is normally collected on Wednesdays but was moved to Thursday that week.

questions.stem: Why was Mr. Hayashi's recycling bin not emptied?

options.A: Packaging kept the lid from closing.
options.B: It was placed at the curb too late.
options.C: It contained items that cannot be recycled.
options.D: It was too heavy to lift safely.

questions.explanation: The notice shows that the lid was not fully closed, and Mr. Hayashi explains that packaging from a furniture delivery would not fit inside the bin, so (A) is correct. The other reasons listed on the notice, (B), (C), and (D), were not checked.

questions.stem: When will Mr. Hayashi most likely take his cardboard to the recycling center?
questions.explanation: Mr. Hayashi says the weekend would be best for him, and the schedule shows the recycling center is open Tuesday through Saturday, so Saturday is the only weekend day he can go (C). The center is closed on Sundays (A) and Mondays (B), and it closes at 4:00 P.M., before most weekday evenings (D).

questions.stem: What is one thing Mr. Hayashi asks about?

options.A: The cost of a larger recycling bin
options.B: The location of the recycling center
options.C: The reason his bin was not emptied
options.D: A possible change to his collection day

questions.explanation: Mr. Hayashi asks whether it is true that collection on his street will move to a different day next year, so (D) is correct. He does not ask about a larger bin (A) or where the center is (B), and he already understands why his bin was not emptied (C).

docs.title: Web page
docs.text:
www.aldmoorhotel.com/lost-and-found

The Aldmoor Hotel | Lost and Found

Did you leave something behind? Items found in guest rooms and public areas are recorded by our housekeeping team and stored securely for 60 days. Valuable items, such as jewelry, laptops, and passports, are kept in the hotel safe. Items that are not claimed within 60 days are donated to local charities.

To report a missing item, please e-mail lostandfound@aldmoorhotel.com with a description of the item, the dates of your stay, and where you think you left it. We will reply within two business days.

Items may be collected in person at the front desk at any time, or we can send them to you by courier. Shipping charges are billed to the guest when the parcel is sent:
• Within the country: $15 (up to 2 kg) or $25 (over 2 kg)
• International: $40 (up to 2 kg) or $65 (over 2 kg)

docs.title: Email
docs.text:
To: lostandfound@aldmoorhotel.com
From: Francesca Moretti
Date: March 9
Subject: Items left behind

Hello,

I stayed at the Aldmoor from March 3 to 6 in Room 512, and I believe I left two items behind. The first is a phone charger with a white cable, which I think is still plugged in beside the bed. The second is a gray wool scarf that I wore to dinner in your restaurant on the evening of March 5.

Could you please send whatever you find to my home address, 14 Fairlie Row, Dunstan Bay? I am happy to pay the shipping charges. Alternatively, I will be back in the city for the Westmarch Tourism Forum in April, so I could also pick the items up then.

Thank you for your help.

Francesca Moretti

docs.title: Reply
docs.text:
To: Francesca Moretti
From: Noriko Ishikawa, Housekeeping Manager
Date: March 10
Subject: RE: Items left behind

Dear Ms. Moretti,

Thank you for contacting us. I am pleased to report that our housekeeping staff found your phone charger when they cleaned your room on March 6. Unfortunately, we have not been able to locate your scarf. I have checked with the staff who worked on the evening of March 5, and no scarf was turned in. We will contact you right away if it is found.

We can send the charger to you this week, and a fee of $15 will be charged to the credit card you used during your stay. However, since you mentioned that you will be returning to the city soon, you may prefer to collect it from the front desk then and avoid the charge. Please let me know which option you would like.

Best regards,
