questions.stem: According to the web page, what happens to items that are not claimed within 60 days?

options.B: They are mailed to the guest's home address.
options.C: They are moved to the hotel safe.
options.D: They are sold at a public auction.

questions.explanation: The web page states that items not claimed within 60 days are donated to local charities, so (A) is correct. Items are sent to guests only on request (B), the safe is used for valuable items from the start (C), and no auction is mentioned (D).

questions.stem: Why did Ms. Moretti write to the hotel?

options.A: To extend her reservation at the hotel
options.B: To complain about a meal in the restaurant
options.C: To ask for help recovering some belongings
options.D: To book a room for a conference in April

questions.explanation: Ms. Moretti writes that she left two items behind and asks the hotel to send whatever it finds, so (C) is correct. Her stay has already ended (A), she mentions the restaurant only as the place she wore her scarf (B), and she does not ask to book a room (D).

questions.stem: Where was the item that has not been found most likely left?
questions.explanation: Ms. Ishikawa says the scarf has not been found, and Ms. Moretti wrote that she wore it to dinner in the hotel restaurant on March 5, so (B) is correct. The charger, which was found, was left in Room 512 (A), and neither the front desk (C) nor the forum (D) is connected with the scarf.

questions.stem: Why would Ms. Moretti be charged $15 to have her charger sent to her?

options.A: It will be sent by an express courier service.
options.B: It is being shipped to an address abroad.
options.C: It had to be kept in the hotel safe.
options.D: It is a small parcel being sent within the country.

questions.explanation: According to the web page, $15 is the fee for a parcel of up to 2 kg sent within the country, which matches the charge in Ms. Ishikawa's e-mail, so (D) is correct. No express service is mentioned (A), international parcels cost at least $40 (B), and storage in the safe has nothing to do with the fee (C).

questions.stem: If Ms. Moretti follows Ms. Ishikawa's suggestion, when will she most likely get her charger?

options.B: During a trip to the city in April

questions.explanation: Ms. Ishikawa suggests collecting the charger at the front desk when Ms. Moretti returns to the city, and Ms. Moretti wrote that she will be back for the Westmarch Tourism Forum in April, so (B) is correct. Two business days is the hotel's reply time (A), March 10 is the date of the reply (C), and unclaimed items are donated after 60 days (D).

directions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given below each sentence. Select the best answer to complete the sentence. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

questions.stem: The keynote speaker, _____ presentation on sustainable packaging drew the largest crowd of the conference, has been invited back next year.
questions.explanation: Why: The gap is followed by a noun (presentation) that belongs to the speaker, so the possessive relative pronoun “whose” is needed; “who” and “whom” cannot come directly before a noun like this.

questions.stem: _____ the fabric shipment arrived two days late, the boutique was still able to launch its autumn collection on schedule.
questions.explanation: Why: The two clauses contrast (late delivery vs. launch on schedule), so the concessive conjunction “Although” fits; “Because” would wrongly present the delay as the reason for the on-time launch.

questions.stem: Passengers were _____ to learn that the new express rail service would reduce their travel time by almost half.
questions.explanation: Why: People who feel an emotion are described with the -ed participle, so “pleased” is correct; “pleasing” describes the thing that causes the feeling.

questions.stem: Ms. Okafor has asked the design team to _____ the brochure layout before it is sent to the printer on Thursday.
questions.explanation: Why: After “to” in “asked … to ___ the layout”, a base-form verb that takes an object is required, so “finalize” is correct; the other choices are an adjective, an adverb and a noun.

questions.stem: Visitors may pay for parking at the machine next to the main entrance _____ through the Harbor Mall mobile application.
questions.explanation: Why: The sentence presents two alternative ways to pay, so “or” is correct; “nor” requires a negative such as “neither”, and “but” and “so” do not express alternatives.

questions.stem: The list of approved suppliers _____ updated every quarter by the purchasing department and posted on the company intranet.
questions.explanation: Why: The subject is the singular noun “list” (not “suppliers”), so the singular verb “is” is needed; “are” is the trap that agrees with the nearer plural noun.

questions.stem: Applicants for the regional sales manager position must submit _____ a cover letter and two letters of reference by March 15.
questions.explanation: Why: The pair is joined by “and”, which goes with “both”; “either” pairs with “or” and “neither” with “nor”.

questions.stem: All safety inspections at the Dunmore Bridge construction site must _____ by a certified structural engineer.
questions.explanation: Why: Inspections do not conduct anything; they are conducted by an engineer, so the passive “be conducted” is required after “must”.

questions.stem: The latest software update is expected to significantly _____ the time needed to process customer refund requests.
questions.explanation: Why: After “to” (and the adverb “significantly”) a verb taking the object “the time” is needed, so “shorten” is correct.

questions.stem: Mr. Delgado usually prefers to book _____ own flights rather than use the travel agency recommended by the company.
questions.explanation: Why: Only a possessive adjective can come before “own flights”, so “his” is correct; “himself” is a reflexive pronoun and cannot modify a noun.

questions.stem: The hotel manager agreed _____ the conference room rental fee for groups of more than fifty guests.
questions.explanation: Why: The verb “agree” is followed by a to-infinitive, so “to reduce” is correct; “agreed reducing” is ungrammatical.

questions.stem: _____ employee who attends Friday’s data security workshop will receive a certificate of completion from the IT department.
questions.explanation: Why: The noun “employee” is singular and the verb is “attends”, so “Every” is needed; “All”, “Most” and “Several” require a plural noun.

questions.stem: Varentis Pharmaceuticals has received _____ from national regulators to begin selling its new allergy medication next spring.
questions.explanation: Why: Companies receive “approval” from regulators before selling a product; “approach” looks similar but does not make sense here.

questions.stem: The marketing director praised the event team for its careful _____ to detail during the product launch in Seoul.
questions.explanation: Why: After the adjective “careful” a noun is needed, and the fixed expression is “attention to detail”.

questions.stem: Tickets for the Milan Designers’ Showcase sold out _____ after they became available on the event’s Web site.
questions.explanation: Why: “Shortly after” means “soon after” and is a common collocation; “nearly after” and “closely after” are not idiomatic here.

questions.stem: The new staff lounge is located _____ the cafeteria and the mail room on the second floor of the building.
questions.explanation: Why: “Between” is used with two things joined by “and” (the cafeteria and the mail room); “among” is used for three or more.

questions.stem: If the contractor _____ the flooring materials by Friday, the renovation of the showroom will be completed on time.
questions.explanation: Why: The main clause uses “will be completed”, so this is a first conditional and the if-clause takes the simple present “delivers”.

questions.stem: Ms. Petrova’s proposal to open a second warehouse was _____ received by the board, which approved it without changes.
questions.explanation: Why: An adverb is needed to modify the verb “was received”, so “enthusiastically” is correct.

questions.stem: Since joining Carrow Engineering in 2019, Mr. Tanaka _____ three major bridge projects in the region.
questions.explanation: Why: “Since + past point” describes a period continuing up to now, so the present perfect “has managed” is required.

questions.stem: _____ heavy snowfall, all afternoon flights from Oslo to Helsinki have been delayed by at least two hours.
questions.explanation: Why: The snowfall is the cause of the delays, so “Due to” fits; “In spite of” expresses the opposite relationship.

questions.stem: The newly renovated Harbor Hotel offers _____ more spacious guest rooms than any other hotel in the downtown area.
questions.explanation: Why: Only a degree adverb such as "considerably" (or much, far) can strengthen a comparative like "more spacious"; "very more" and "too more" are ungrammatical, and "such" needs a noun phrase ("such spacious rooms").

questions.stem: Please _____ the attached invoice carefully and let us know if you have any questions about the charges.
questions.explanation: Why: You “review” a document; “reply” and “respond” need “to”, and you “notify” a person, not an invoice.

questions.stem: By the time the new factory in Monterrey opens next spring, the company _____ more than two hundred workers.
questions.explanation: Why: “By the time … next spring” refers to an action completed before a future point, so the future perfect “will have hired” is needed.

questions.stem: The quarterly sales figures _____ to all regional managers yesterday afternoon, along with the new targets.
questions.explanation: Why: The figures are the things being sent, and “yesterday” requires the past, so the past passive “were sent” is correct.

questions.stem: The museum’s special exhibition on maritime trade will remain open _____ the end of October.
questions.explanation: Why: "Remain open" describes a continuing situation, so "until" marks when it ends. "By" is the trap: it gives a deadline for a completed action ("finish by the end of October"), not the end point of an ongoing state.

questions.stem: The organizing committee is considering _____ the annual logistics conference to a larger venue in Singapore.
questions.explanation: Why: The verb “consider” is followed by a gerund, so “moving” is correct.

questions.stem: Assembly Line 2 has been running _____ since the technicians replaced its faulty sensors last week.
questions.explanation: Why: A machine that has been repaired is now running "flawlessly" (without any problems). "Reluctantly" describes a person's attitude, and "tightly" and "considerably" do not describe how a machine operates.

questions.stem: Online orders placed before noon are _____ for same-day delivery to addresses within the city limits.
questions.explanation: Why: The collocation is “eligible for” (meeting the conditions for something); “capable” takes “of”, and “responsible” and “reliable” do not fit the meaning.

questions.stem: The client requested several changes to the floor plan; _____ , the architects revised the drawings within a week.
questions.explanation: Why: The revision is the natural result of the request, so “accordingly” (= as a result) fits; “nevertheless” would signal a contrast.

questions.stem: The survey results show that most customers find the new online checkout process much more _____ than the old one.
questions.explanation: Why: A checkout process that customers find easy to understand and use is "intuitive." "Exhaustive" (thorough, complete), "cooperative" (willing to help) and "tentative" (not certain) do not describe how easy a process is to use.

directions: Read the texts that follow. A word, phrase, or sentence is missing in parts of each text. Four answer choices for each question are given below the text. Select the best answer to complete the text. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

docs.title: Expo-Lite Portable Display Stand — Setup Guide
docs.text:
Thank you for purchasing the Expo-Lite Portable Display Stand. Before you begin, check that all of the parts shown on the enclosed parts sheet are in the carrying case.
131
any pieces are missing, please contact our customer care team at 1-800-555-0143 before attempting to assemble the stand.
First, unfold the aluminum frame and lock each of the four hinges into place. Next, attach the printed fabric panel
132
it firmly against the hook-and-loop strips that run along the top and side bars. Then slide the two lighting arms into the slots at the top of the frame. The lights
133
by the rechargeable battery pack included with the stand, so no electrical outlet is needed at your event.
The entire stand can be set up by one person in less than ten minutes.
134

questions.explanation: Why: The sentence describes a condition (pieces missing) and what to do in that case, so “If” is correct; “Unless” reverses the meaning and “Although” signals contrast.
Why: “By + -ing” explains how the panel is attached, so “by pressing” is correct; the base form “press” would create a second main verb without a conjunction.
Why: The lights receive power from the battery pack, so the passive “are powered” is needed; the present tense matches the general description in the rest of the guide.

options.A: An electrician will need to connect the lights to an outlet.
options.B: Two or more people are required to lift the frame safely.
options.C: The fabric panel should be attached before the frame is unfolded.
options.D: To take it down, simply follow these steps in reverse order.

questions.explanation: Why: After explaining how to set the stand up, the guide logically ends by explaining how to take it down. Each distractor contradicts the guide: it says no outlet is needed, that one person can set the stand up, and that the frame is unfolded first.

docs.text:
Dear Ms. Suzuki,
Thank you for choosing Threadworks Tailoring for your custom suit. I am writing to let you know that the charcoal wool fabric you selected is
135
out of stock at our supplier in Leeds. The supplier expects to receive a new shipment in about three weeks.
136
, your suit would be ready for collection on 20 June instead of 1 June as originally planned.
If this delay is inconvenient, we would be happy to make your suit from a similar fabric produced by another mill.
137
Each of them has the same weight and finish as your original choice, and there would be no change in price.
Please let me know which option you
138
by Friday so that we can proceed with your order.
Best regards,
Liam O’Connell
Threadworks Tailoring

questions.explanation: Why: An adverb is needed to modify the adjective phrase “out of stock”, so “temporarily” is correct; the next sentence (a new shipment in three weeks) confirms the shortage is not permanent.
Why: The later completion date is a consequence of the fabric shortage described before it, so “As a result” is the logical connector; “Even so” would signal an unexpected contrast.

options.A: Unfortunately, no similar fabrics are available at this time.
options.B: I have attached photographs of three fabrics in the same shade.
options.C: Many customers prefer lighter fabrics for summer events.
options.D: Your measurements were taken by our senior tailor.

questions.explanation: Why: The next sentence begins "Each of them", which needs a plural referent; the photographs of three alternative fabrics provide it and follow naturally from the offer of a similar fabric. (A) contradicts that offer.
Why: The subject of the clause is “you”, so the base present form “prefer” is required; “prefers” is for third-person singular subjects and “preference” is a noun.

docs.title: Notice to All Tenants of the Wexford Business Tower
docs.text:
Please be advised that both passenger elevators in the Wexford Business Tower will be out of service from 7:00 A.M. on Saturday, 8 June, until 6:00 P.M. on Sunday, 9 June. During this time, technicians
139
new digital control systems in both elevator cars. The upgrade will reduce waiting times and make the elevators more energy efficient.
We understand that this work may cause some
140
for tenants who plan to work in the building over the weekend. The stairways will remain open at all times, and the freight elevator at the rear of the building will remain
141
for tenants who need to move heavy equipment or deliveries.
142
Thank you for your patience while we improve the building’s facilities.
— Wexford Property Management

questions.explanation: Why: The work takes place on dates that have not yet arrived (the elevators “will be out of service”), so the future “will install” is required.
Why: After the determiner “some”, a noun is needed as the object of “cause”, so “inconvenience” is correct.
Why: The freight elevator can still be used, so it will “remain available”; “potential” and “former” do not describe something that can currently be used.

options.A: However, it must be reserved in advance through the management office.
options.B: The new control systems were installed last weekend.
options.C: Tenants are reminded that smoking is not permitted in the lobby.
options.D: The tower was completed more than thirty years ago.

questions.explanation: Why: “It” refers to the freight elevator mentioned just before, and “However” adds a condition on its use; the sentence about systems installed “last weekend” contradicts the future timing of the work.

docs.text:
Beginning Monday, 10 February, all visitors to the Halvorsen Pharmaceuticals research campus must be
143
by an employee at all times. Visitors will also be required to sign in at the main reception desk and to wear a visitor badge
144
their stay. Badges must be returned to reception when visitors leave the campus.
These measures are being introduced to protect the confidential research data stored in our laboratories.

Similar procedures have already been adopted at our production site in Rotterdam, and contractors who work on campus regularly will be issued long-term passes.
If you are expecting a guest, please notify reception at least one working day in advance so that a badge can be prepared.

you have any questions about the new procedures, contact the Facilities Office at extension 4410.

questions.explanation: Why: After “must be”, the past participle forms the passive: visitors are accompanied by an employee, so “accompanied” is correct.
Why: “Throughout their stay” means during the whole visit; “among”, “beside” and “onto” do not express duration.

options.A: Our cafeteria menu will change next month.
options.B: Visitors were welcome to tour the laboratories freely.
options.C: Research data can be downloaded from our public Web site.
options.D: They will also bring us in line with the latest industry standards.

questions.explanation: Why: “They” refers to “these measures”, and “also” adds a second reason for introducing them; the sentence about public research data contradicts the goal of protecting confidential data.

Why: “Should you have any questions” is an inverted conditional meaning “If you have any questions”; “Were” and “Had” cannot be followed by the base verb “have” here, and “Unless” reverses the meaning.

directions: In this part you will read a selection of texts, such as magazine and newspaper articles, e-mails, and instant messages. Each text or set of texts is followed by several questions. Select the best answer for each question and mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

docs.text:
Diego Ramírez 9:12 A.M.: Hi Aisha, I’m at the Lakeview Convention Center setting up our booth. The banners haven’t turned up.
Aisha Rahman 9:14 A.M.: That’s strange. The print shop promised they’d be delivered straight to the loading dock this morning.
Diego Ramírez 9:15 A.M.: I asked the dock manager. Nothing has come in under our company name.
Aisha Rahman 9:17 A.M.: Let me call the print shop now.
Aisha Rahman 9:26 A.M.: OK, their driver is stuck in traffic on the ring road. He should be with you by 10:30.
Diego Ramírez 9:27 A.M.: The doors open to the public at 11:00.
Aisha Rahman 9:28 A.M.: I know it’s tight. Could you get the tables and product samples arranged in the meantime?
Diego Ramírez 9:29 A.M.: Already on it.

questions.stem: What problem does Mr. Ramírez report?

options.A: A booth was assigned to another company.
options.C: Some items have not been delivered.
options.D: The loading dock has been closed.

questions.explanation: Why: Mr. Ramírez says the banners “haven’t turned up” and nothing has come in at the dock; the loading dock is mentioned but is not closed.

questions.stem: At 9:29 A.M., what does Mr. Ramírez most likely mean when he writes, “Already on it”?

options.A: He has already called the print shop himself.
options.B: He is driving on the ring road.
options.C: He has already hung the banners.
options.D: He has started preparing the display area.

questions.explanation: Why: He is answering Ms. Rahman’s request to arrange the tables and samples, so he means he is already doing that; Ms. Rahman, not he, called the print shop, and the banners have not arrived.

docs.text:
Dear Ms. Lindqvist,
Thank you for supporting the Aldermoor Museum of Art as a member for the past three years. Your annual membership will expire on 30 April. Renewing is easy: simply complete the enclosed form and return it in the prepaid envelope, or renew online at www.aldermoorart.org/members.

We hope to continue welcoming you to the museum in the year ahead.

Martin Oyelaran
Membership Coordinator

questions.stem: Why was the letter sent?

options.A: To announce the opening of a café
options.B: To thank a donor for a gift
options.C: To request payment of an overdue fee
options.D: To encourage a member to renew

questions.explanation: Why: The letter reminds Ms. Lindqvist that her membership expires on 30 April and explains how to renew; the café and exhibition are mentioned only as membership benefits.

questions.stem: According to the letter, what will Ms. Lindqvist receive if she renews by 31 March?

options.A: A gift from the museum shop
options.B: A ticket to the spring preview

questions.explanation: Why: Members who renew before 31 March get “two complimentary guest passes” for friends or family, which means free admission for two visitors. The letter mentions only a shop discount, not a gift, and preview invitations are a benefit all members already receive.

docs.title: Quillsoft Launches ShiftMate Scheduling App
docs.text:
TORONTO (2 September) — Quillsoft Inc. today announced the launch of ShiftMate, a scheduling application designed for restaurants, retail stores, and other small businesses with hourly staff. ShiftMate allows managers to build weekly schedules in minutes and lets employees exchange shifts with coworkers directly from their phones, subject to a manager’s approval.
“Small business owners told us they were spending up to six hours a week on staff schedules,” said Quillsoft CEO Daniel Hoffmann. “ShiftMate reduces that time dramatically.”
The app was tested for eight months by more than 300 businesses across Canada before its public release. ShiftMate is free for teams of up to ten employees; larger teams pay $3 per employee per month. It is available now for both major mobile platforms, and a desktop version is planned for early next year.

questions.stem: What is indicated about ShiftMate?

options.A: It is intended mainly for large corporations.
options.B: It lets workers trade shifts with one another.
options.C: It can currently be used on desktop computers.
options.D: It was developed in less than a week.

questions.explanation: Why: The release says employees can “exchange shifts with coworkers”; the desktop version is only planned, and “six hours a week” refers to time owners spend on schedules.

questions.stem: What is stated about the price of ShiftMate?

options.A: Small teams can use it at no cost.
options.B: Charges depend on the number of hours worked.
options.D: The monthly fee will increase next year.

questions.explanation: Why: ShiftMate “is free for teams of up to ten employees”; larger teams pay per employee, not per hour worked.

docs.title: Old Town Food Walk, Lisbon ★★★★☆
docs.text:
My colleagues and I booked this three-hour tour on the last evening of a week-long business trip, and it turned out to be the highlight of our stay. Our guide, Rui, met us at the fountain in Praça da Figueira at exactly 6:00 P.M. and led us to six family-run establishments, where we sampled everything from grilled sardines to custard tarts. Rui clearly knew the owners personally, and his stories about the history of each neighborhood made the walks between stops go by quickly.
My only complaint concerns the booking information. The company’s Web site stated that drinks were included, but at two of the stops we had to pay for our own beverages. When I e-mailed the company afterward, a representative apologized and explained that the site had not been updated since the tour changed its menu. She offered me a 20 percent discount on a future tour, which was a kind gesture, although I am not sure when I will next be in Lisbon.
A word of advice: wear comfortable shoes, as some of the streets are steep and cobbled. I would recommend this tour to anyone visiting the city.

options.A: She was taking a cooking course.
options.C: She was leading a tour group.
options.D: She was on a business trip.

questions.explanation: Why: She booked the tour “on the last evening of a week-long business trip”; she joined a tour but did not lead one.

options.A: He owns one of the restaurants on the tour.
options.B: He arrived late at the meeting point.
options.C: He advised the group to wear comfortable shoes.
options.D: He knows the owners of the businesses visited.

questions.explanation: Why: The reviewer says Rui “clearly knew the owners personally”; he met the group “at exactly 6:00 P.M.”, and the shoe advice comes from the reviewer herself.

options.A: The distances between stops were too long.
options.B: Information online was out of date.
options.C: The food portions were too small.
options.D: The company refused to give her a refund.

questions.explanation: Why: The Web site said drinks were included but had “not been updated”; the company actually offered her a discount rather than refusing her.

docs.title: Skyreach Air to Expand Regional Network
docs.text:
PERTH (18 August) — Skyreach Air, a regional carrier based in Perth, will add four new routes to its network beginning in November, the airline announced on Monday. The new services will connect Perth with Geraldton, Esperance, Broome, and Kalgoorlie, towns that until now have been served mainly by small charter operators.
To operate the routes, Skyreach has leased three turboprop aircraft, each seating 72 passengers. The airline is also hiring 40 new staff members, including pilots, cabin crew, and ground personnel. According to chief executive Olivia Brennan, most of the new ground staff will work at the regional airports rather than in Perth.
“Residents of these communities have been asking for affordable, scheduled flights for years,” Ms. Brennan said. “Many of them travel to Perth regularly for business meetings, university classes, and family visits.”
Introductory fares start at $129 one way and will go on sale on the airline’s Web site on 1 September. Flights to Broome will run daily, while the other three routes will operate four times a week.

options.D: They will be filled by charter operators.

Dear Dr. Haidari,
Thank you again for agreeing to speak at this year’s International Pharmaceutical Packaging Forum in Vienna. Your session, “Reducing Plastic in Blister Packs,” is scheduled for Thursday, 22 May, at 10:30 A.M. in Hall B. Each speaker is allotted 40 minutes, including 10 minutes for questions from the audience.
As agreed, the Forum will cover your accommodation for the nights of 21 and 22 May at the Hotel Lindenhof, a short walk from the conference center. Speakers are responsible for booking their own flights; however, we will reimburse economy-class airfare of up to €400 upon receipt of your ticket invoice.
Please send your presentation slides to me by 12 May so that our technical team can load them onto the computer in the hall. If you require any additional equipment, let me know as soon as possible.
Finally, all speakers are warmly invited to the opening reception, which will be held at the conference center on the evening of 21 May from 7:00 to 9:00 P.M. Please tell me by 12 May whether you plan to attend.
Best regards,
Jonas Becker
Speaker Coordinator

Dear Mr. Becker,
Thank you for the details. I have booked my flights and attached the invoice; the round-trip economy fare came to €465. I understand that the Forum’s contribution is limited.
I have one request. My colleague Tobias Lund, who led the laboratory testing described in my presentation, will also be attending the Forum. Would it be possible for him to join me on stage for the question period? He can answer technical questions far better than I can. He has already registered as a regular attendee, so he has his own conference pass.
In addition, I plan to show a short video clip during my talk, so I will need speakers connected to the hall computer. My slides will reach you before your deadline. Unfortunately, because of a prior commitment, I will not be able to arrive in Vienna until the evening before my session. I am afraid I will probably miss most of the opening reception as a result, but I would be glad to join if my flight lands on time.
Kind regards,
Farida Haidari

docs.title: Express Trains Coming to Northline
docs.text:
WESTBRIDGE (4 August) — Commuters on the Northline rail route will soon have a faster option. Beginning Monday, 1 September, Westbridge Regional Transit (WRT) will introduce express trains that stop only at Harlow, Fenton Park, and Central Station, cutting the journey from Harlow to the city center from 58 minutes to 41.
The express trains will run during the morning and evening rush hours on weekdays only. Regular trains, which stop at all eleven stations on the line, will continue to operate throughout the day.
WRT spokesperson Chidi Okonkwo said the change responds to rapid population growth in Harlow, where several large housing developments have been completed over the past two years. “Passenger numbers at Harlow station have doubled since 2023,” he said.
Tickets for express trains will cost the same as those for regular service. In addition, WRT will launch a new monthly pass priced at $140, allowing unlimited travel on both express and regular trains. Riders who buy the pass before 1 September will receive a 10 percent discount.
The express service is the first stage of a larger upgrade of the Northline. WRT also plans to expand the car park at Harlow station by 150 spaces by the end of the year and to lengthen the platforms at Fenton Park by 2027 so that longer trains can be used.

Hello,
I live in Harlow and work in an office near Central Station. My workday begins at 8:15 A.M. At the moment, I take the 6:55 regular train, which gets me there on time but means getting up very early. I was delighted to read about the new express service in the newspaper, and several of my neighbors are also planning to switch to it.
I have two questions. First, will I be allowed to bring my folding bicycle on express trains, as I currently do on regular trains? Second, I bought a regular monthly ticket on 1 August that is valid until the end of this month. If I purchase the new pass for September today, will I still receive the discount?
Thank you,
Rosa Villanueva

Tickets and monthly passes can be purchased from station ticket machines or through the WRT mobile app. Times are subject to change; please check wrt-transit.com for the latest information.

Each participant receives a certificate of completion at the end of the day. Our center is a ten-minute walk from Britomart Station, and free parking is available behind the building. Workshops often fill up quickly, so early registration is recommended.

questions.stem: What is indicated about Brightpath workshops?

options.D: They are taught by a single instructor.

questions.explanation: Why: The brochure says the fee “includes lunch”; all workshops are on Saturdays at a training center, so they are neither weekday nor online events.

questions.stem: Why did Mr. Taufa pay $442?

options.B: He registered for more than one workshop.
options.C: His company is an official Brightpath partner.
options.D: He asked for a vegetarian lunch.

questions.explanation: Why: He signed up for two $260 workshops (form), and the brochure gives 15% off for two or more: $520 minus 15% is $442. Nothing mentions an early-registration deadline.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the e-mail?
questions.explanation: Why: Ms. Whitfield writes to say the Project Management workshop has been moved to 3 May; the instructor is mentioned only as the reason for the change.

questions.stem: What is suggested about the refund offered in the e-mail?

options.A: It will be paid by check within a week.
options.B: It covers both of Mr. Taufa’s workshops.
options.C: It is an exception to Brightpath’s usual policy.
options.D: It will be given as credit toward a future workshop.

The refund is only for Project Management Essentials, not both workshops, and it is a full refund, not a credit.

directions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given below each sentence. Select the best answer to complete the sentence. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

questions.stem: Visitors to the Tavira Energy plant must sign in at the security desk located _____ the main entrance.
questions.explanation: Why: “Beside” means “next to” and correctly locates the desk in relation to one entrance; “between” needs two points of reference, “among” needs a group, and “throughout” means “in every part of”.

questions.stem: Applications for the regional agricultural innovation grant must be submitted no later than 5:00 P.M. _____ Friday, 14 March.
questions.explanation: Why: Days and dates take “on” (on Friday, 14 March); “at” is used for clock times such as 5:00 P.M., which is the trap, and “in” is used for months and years.

questions.stem: Since the start of the year, Veltro Motors _____ its production of electric delivery vans by nearly 30 percent.
questions.explanation: Why: “Since the start of the year” describes a period that began in the past and continues to now, so the present perfect “has increased” is needed; “increasing” is not a finite verb.

questions.stem: The marketing team worked _____ to finish the campaign materials before the product launch on Monday.
questions.explanation: Why: “Worked tirelessly” (worked very hard without stopping) is a natural collocation that fits a deadline context; “narrowly”, “vaguely” and “sparsely” do not describe how someone works toward a goal.

questions.stem: _____ the conference hall was fully booked, the organizers arranged a second room with a live video feed.
questions.explanation: Why: The first clause gives the reason for the second (the hall was full, so a second room was arranged), so “Because” is correct; “Although” would wrongly signal a contrast.

questions.stem: Each of the tour packages _____ airport transfers, daily breakfast, and a guided walk through the old town.
questions.explanation: Why: The subject is “Each”, which is singular, so the singular verb “includes” is required; “include” agrees with the nearby plural “packages”, which is the trap.

questions.stem: All customer complaints about dropped calls _____ to the network engineering team within 24 hours.
questions.explanation: Why: Complaints do not forward anything; they are sent by someone, so the passive “are forwarded” is needed. The active forms “forward” and “have forwarded” would need an object.

questions.stem: The hotel’s general manager expressed her _____ to the staff for their hard work during the busy holiday season.
questions.explanation: Why: After the possessive “her”, a noun is required, so “appreciation” is correct; the other choices are a verb, an adjective and an adverb.

questions.stem: Farmers _____ crops were damaged by last month’s hailstorm may apply for emergency assistance through the regional office.
questions.explanation: Why: The crops belong to the farmers, so the possessive relative pronoun “whose” is needed before the noun “crops”; “who”, “whom” and “which” cannot introduce a noun in this way.

questions.stem: _____ rising fuel costs, Palmera Tours has raised the price of its coastal bus excursions by five dollars.
questions.explanation: Why: Rising fuel costs are the cause of the price increase, so “Due to” is correct; “In spite of” would suggest the price rose despite the costs, which is illogical.

questions.stem: The new billing software has been _____ tested to make sure that customer data remains secure.
questions.explanation: Why: “Thoroughly tested” (tested completely and carefully) is a standard collocation; “shortly” means “soon” and does not describe how testing is done.

questions.stem: Registered attendees may pick up their badges _____ at the information desk or at one of the self-service kiosks in the lobby.
questions.explanation: Why: The pair is completed by “or”, so “either” is needed; “neither” pairs with “nor”, “both” with “and”, and “not only” with “but also”.

questions.stem: Of all the solar panel models tested, the Helion X4 produced the _____ amount of electricity on cloudy days.
questions.explanation: Why: “Of all the models” and “the” signal a comparison among more than two items, so the superlative “greatest” is required; “greater” compares only two.

questions.stem: Guests have described the staff at the Coralina Resort as extremely _____ and quick to respond to requests.
questions.explanation: Why: After “described … as extremely”, an adjective is needed, parallel with “quick”; “helpfully” is an adverb and “helpfulness” is a noun.

questions.stem: The results of the customer survey were _____ , as more than 90 percent of respondents rated the service as excellent.
questions.explanation: Why: Results cause a feeling in others, so the -ing adjective “encouraging” is correct; “encouraged” describes a person who feels encouragement.

questions.stem: Mr. Balogun prefers to review the supplier contracts _____ rather than rely on a summary from the legal team.
questions.explanation: Why: "Himself" is an emphatic reflexive: Mr. Balogun reads the contracts personally instead of relying on the legal team. "Him" and "he" cannot stand alone after the object "the supplier contracts," and "his" would need a noun after it.

questions.stem: Every Veltro vehicle comes with a _____ warranty that covers all parts and labor for five years.
questions.explanation: Why: A “comprehensive warranty” is one that covers everything, which matches “covers all parts and labor”; “numerous” needs a plural noun, and “spacious” and “frequent” do not describe a warranty.

questions.stem: _____ offering discounted rail passes, the city tourism board provides free walking maps at every major station.
questions.explanation: Why: The board does two things (offers passes and provides maps), so “In addition to” is correct; “Because of” would wrongly present the passes as the cause of the maps.

questions.stem: _____ employee must complete the online safety course before entering the turbine maintenance area.
questions.explanation: Why: The singular noun “employee” and the singular verb “must complete” require “Every”; “All”, “Few” and “Most” are used with plural countable nouns.

questions.stem: If the shipment of seed potatoes _____ by Thursday, the farm cooperative will begin planting next week.
questions.explanation: Why: In a first conditional, the if-clause takes the present simple while the main clause uses “will”, so “arrives” is correct; “will arrive” is not used after “if” here.

questions.stem: The new mobile plan offers unlimited data; _____ , it costs less than our previous premium package.
questions.explanation: Why: The second clause adds another advantage to the first, so “moreover” is correct; “therefore” would wrongly suggest that unlimited data causes the lower price.

questions.stem: Only a _____ of the vehicles recalled last spring still need to be inspected at authorized dealerships.
questions.explanation: Why: “Vehicles” is a plural countable noun, so “a few of” is correct; “a little” and “much” are used with uncountable nouns, and “several” cannot follow “a”.

questions.stem: The event planner hopes to _____ costs by booking the venue and catering from a single supplier.
questions.explanation: Why: After “hopes to”, a base-form verb that can take the object “costs” is needed, so “minimize” is correct; the other choices are an adjective, a noun/adjective and an adverb.

questions.stem: The upgraded fiber network allows customers to download large files _____ faster than before.
questions.explanation: Why: An adverb is needed to modify the comparative “faster”, so “considerably” is correct; “considerable” is an adjective and cannot modify another modifier.

questions.stem: The regional energy authority has agreed to _____ the approval process for small wind farm projects so that permits can be issued within weeks rather than months.
questions.explanation: Why: "Streamline" means to make a process simpler and faster, which matches permits being issued "within weeks rather than months"; "prolong" (make longer) is the opposite, and "consume" and "resemble" do not fit "the approval process."

questions.stem: Before signing the agreement, Ms. Quispe asked the supplier to _____ the delivery terms outlined in section 4.
questions.explanation: Why: “Clarify the delivery terms” means make them clearer, and “clarify” takes a direct object; “respond”, “agree” and “arrive” need a preposition (respond to, agree to/on) or take no object.

questions.stem: The hotel’s rooftop restaurant will be closed for repairs until May. _____ , guests may enjoy dinner in the lobby café.
questions.explanation: Why: The second sentence tells guests what to do during the period before the restaurant reopens, so “In the meantime” is correct; “Otherwise” would mean “if not”, which does not fit.

questions.stem: By the time the trade fair opens next month, our team _____ all of the promotional displays.
questions.explanation: Why: “By the time … next month” refers to an action completed before a future point, so the future perfect “will have assembled” is correct; “assembled” and “has assembled” do not refer to the future.

questions.stem: Given the _____ demand for its fiber service, Brightline Telecom plans to double the number of its installation crews by June.
questions.explanation: Why: "Surging demand" (demand that is rising quickly) explains why the company would double its crews; "marginal" (very small) and "tentative" (uncertain) demand would not justify expansion, and "reluctant" describes people, not demand.

questions.stem: _____ the new booking system been tested more thoroughly, the double reservations last weekend could have been avoided.
questions.explanation: Why: This is an inverted third conditional (= If the system had been tested…): "been" needs "had," and "could have been avoided" refers to the past. "If" would need "had" after it, "Should" is used for future possibilities, and "Were" cannot be followed by "been."

directions: Read the texts that follow. A word, phrase, or sentence is missing in parts of each text. Four answer choices for each question are given below the text. Select the best answer to complete the text. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

docs.title: Brightline Fiber Home Gateway — Quick Start Guide
docs.text:
Thank you for choosing Brightline Fiber. Your new home gateway combines a modem and a wireless router in a single device. Setup takes about fifteen minutes and requires no special tools.
First, connect the gray cable from the wall outlet to the port marked FIBER on the back of the gateway.
131
, plug the power adapter into an electrical outlet and press the power switch. The indicator light on the front of the gateway will flash blue while the device
132
to our network.
Once the light turns solid white, you can join the wireless network. Simply select the network name on your computer or phone and enter the password. Both are printed on the
133
attached to the bottom of the gateway.
If the light is still flashing after ten minutes, restart the gateway by holding the reset button for five seconds.
134

questions.explanation: Why: The guide lists steps in order (“First, … Then, …”), so the sequencing word “Then” is correct; “Instead” and “However” would wrongly suggest the second step replaces or contrasts with the first.

Why: The guide uses the present tense to describe what happens during setup (“will flash … while the device connects”), and after “while” in a future context the present simple is used; the past “connected” does not fit the rest of the instructions.
Why: Something “printed on” and “attached to the bottom of the gateway” is a label; a brochure, envelope or schedule would not be attached to the device.

options.A: Your first monthly bill will include a one-time activation fee.
options.B: Should the problem continue, please call our support line at 1-800-555-0172.
options.C: For the best signal, place the gateway away from thick walls and metal objects.
options.D: You may also connect a computer directly using a network cable.

questions.explanation: Why: The last paragraph deals with a light that keeps flashing, so the logical final step is what to do if restarting does not help: call support. The signal and network-cable tips are on topic but belong with setup, not troubleshooting, and the billing sentence is unrelated.

docs.title: Greenvale Cooperative to Expand Drone Program
docs.text:
GREENVALE — The Greenvale Farmers’ Cooperative announced on Tuesday that it will expand its crop-monitoring program to all 140 member farms by next spring. Since the pilot program began two years ago, small drones
135
fields of wheat and barley on twelve farms, photographing the crops once a week.
The images help farmers identify areas that need water or fertilizer before problems become visible from the ground.
136
, participating farms reduced their fertilizer use by an average of 18 percent last season.
The expansion will be funded in part by a grant from the provincial agriculture ministry. Members will also pay a small annual fee to cover the
137
of the equipment, including repairs and replacement batteries.
Cooperative director Imani Wekesa said the program has been popular with growers.
138

questions.explanation: Why: “Since the pilot program began two years ago” describes an action continuing from the past to now, so the present perfect “have surveyed” is needed; the passive “are surveyed” does not fit because the drones do the surveying.
Why: Reduced fertilizer use is a consequence of finding problems early, so “As a result” is correct; “Nevertheless” and “In contrast” would signal an opposing idea.
Why: The fee covers “repairs and replacement batteries”, which describes the upkeep (maintenance) of the equipment; the other nouns are not costs that a fee would cover.

options.A: Ms. Wekesa has directed the cooperative for nearly a decade.
options.B: Wheat and barley prices fell sharply at the end of last year.
options.C: The ministry has not yet approved any funding for member farms.
options.D: “Several members have already asked when they can join,” she noted.

questions.explanation: Why: The quotation supports the director's statement that the program is popular with growers. The sentence about her career does not support "popular," the ministry sentence contradicts the grant mentioned earlier, and crop prices are off topic.

docs.title: Nordhaven Power Opens Kestrel Ridge Wind Farm
docs.text:
NORDHAVEN, 3 September — Nordhaven Power today announced the opening of its Kestrel Ridge Wind Farm, the largest
139
energy project in the region. The facility’s 42 turbines will generate enough electricity to supply roughly 60,000 homes each year. The company expects the project to reduce the region’s carbon emissions by about 90,000 tonnes annually.
Construction began in March of last year and was completed two months ahead of schedule.
140
To celebrate the opening, Nordhaven Power will host a community open day at the site on Saturday, 14 September. Visitors can tour the control building and speak
141
engineers about how the turbines operate. Free shuttle buses
142
from Nordhaven train station every thirty minutes beginning at 9:00 A.M.

questions.explanation: Why: An adjective is needed before the noun phrase “energy project”, so “renewable” is correct; “renewal” is a noun, “renew” a verb and “renewably” an adverb.

options.A: The turbines will be installed at the site next spring.
options.B: Nordhaven Power was founded by three engineers in 1987.
options.C: The early finish was largely due to unusually mild winter weather.
options.D: Residents may apply for positions at the company’s new call center.

questions.explanation: Why: The sentence explains why construction finished “ahead of schedule”, referring back to it as “the early finish”; saying the turbines will be installed next spring contradicts the opening of the facility.
Why: “Speak with someone” is the correct pattern for having a conversation; “speak at” refers to an event or place, and “speak by” and “speak among” do not fit before “engineers about”.
Why: The open day takes place in the future (Saturday, 14 September), so the future “will run” is required; “ran” and “have run” refer to the past, and “running” is not a finite verb.

docs.text:
Dear Ms. Haraldsdóttir,
Thank you for selecting the Albaterra Hotel for your company’s sales conference. I am pleased to

questions.explanation: Why: "Pleased to confirm that…" states that the booking has been made. "Assure" and "notify" need a person as object (assure you that / notify you that), and "insist that" does not fit a polite confirmation.

options.A: Our ballroom was recently painted in a lighter color.
options.B: I have enclosed a copy of the lunch menu for both days.
options.C: We look forward to seeing you at our restaurant soon.
options.D: Unfortunately, the conference must be held at another venue.

questions.explanation: Why: The next sentence asks the reader to “review it” and mention dietary requirements, so “it” must refer to a menu; the sentence about another venue contradicts the confirmed booking.
Why: The deposit is an additional piece of information about the booking, so “In addition” is correct; “For instance” would introduce an example and “Instead” a replacement.
Why: An adverb is needed to modify the verb “respond”, so “promptly” is correct; “prompt” is an adjective, “promptness” a noun and “prompted” a past participle.

directions: In this part you will read a selection of texts, such as magazine and newspaper articles, e-mails, and instant messages. Each text or set of texts is followed by several questions. Select the best answer for each question and mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

docs.text:
Lucía Ferreyra 2:14 P.M.: Hi Dmitri. The owner of the blue hatchback just called again. She wants to know if her car will be ready by the end of the day.
Dmitri Volkov 2:16 P.M.: Not yet. We’re still waiting for the brake pads from Hollins Auto Parts. They were supposed to be delivered this morning.
Lucía Ferreyra 2:17 P.M.: She’s leaving on a business trip early tomorrow, so she really needs it tonight. Is there anything we can do?
Dmitri Volkov 2:19 P.M.: Kofi is driving to their warehouse right now.
Lucía Ferreyra 2:20 P.M.: That’s a relief. How long will the job take once he’s back?
Dmitri Volkov 2:21 P.M.: About an hour and a half. She should be able to pick it up by six.
Lucía Ferreyra 2:22 P.M.: Perfect. I’ll call her back and let her know.

questions.stem: Why did the customer call?

options.A: To check on the status of her car
options.C: To order some new brake pads
options.D: To complain about a repair bill

questions.explanation: Why: Ms. Ferreyra says the owner “wants to know if her car will be ready by the end of the day”; brake pads are mentioned, but the garage, not the customer, ordered them.

questions.stem: At 2:19 P.M., what does Mr. Volkov most likely mean when he writes, “Kofi is driving to their warehouse right now”?

options.A: A delivery has just arrived at the garage.
options.B: The customer’s car is being test-driven.
options.C: A coworker is going to pick up the missing parts.
options.D: Kofi will drive the customer to the airport.

questions.explanation: Why: Mr. Volkov is answering “Is there anything we can do?” about the brake pads that were not delivered, so he means Kofi is collecting them from the supplier himself; nothing has arrived yet.

docs.title: Telvaro Brings Coverage to Highland Villages
docs.text:
SAN MIGUEL DE LOS ALTOS — Telvaro Communications has completed the installation of fourteen new cell towers in the Altos highlands, bringing reliable mobile service to more than thirty villages for the first time. Until now, many residents had to drive up to 40 kilometers to make a phone call or send a message.
The project, which cost an estimated $22 million, was partly funded by a national program that encourages companies to extend service to remote communities. Telvaro spokesperson Renata Iturbide said the company chose the area because of its fast-growing tourism industry. “Visitors come for the hiking trails and hot springs, and they expect to stay connected,” she explained.
Local business owners welcome the change. Mateo Quilca, who runs a small guesthouse in the village of Pumaqaqa, says some guests have left early in the past because they could not work remotely. “Now I can finally advertise high-speed service,” he said.
Telvaro plans to install six additional towers in the neighboring Condor Valley next year.

questions.stem: What is the article mainly about?

options.A: The opening of new hiking trails nearby
options.B: Improved phone coverage in remote areas
options.C: A government program for guesthouse owners
options.D: A decline in tourism in the highlands

questions.explanation: Why: The article reports that new towers bring mobile service to remote villages; hiking trails and a national program are mentioned only as details.

questions.stem: According to the article, why did Telvaro select the area?

options.A: Because the number of visitors is rising
options.D: Because it already had several towers

questions.explanation: Why: Ms. Iturbide says the company chose the area “because of its fast-growing tourism industry”; the area had no reliable service before, so it did not already have towers.

docs.title: Explore the Saltmarsh Coast by Rail!
docs.text:
The Saltmarsh Coast Explorer Pass gives you unlimited travel on all regional trains between Port Averly and Kestwick for three, five, or seven consecutive days. Pass holders also enjoy free entry to the Averly Maritime Museum and 15 percent off harbor boat tours in Linmouth.
Prices: 3-day pass $69 • 5-day pass $99 • 7-day pass $129. Children under 12 travel free when accompanied by an adult pass holder.
Passes can be purchased online at www.saltmarshrail.com or at the ticket office of any staffed station. Passes bought online are sent by e-mail and can be shown on a mobile phone.
New this year: Bicycles may be brought on board free of charge on weekdays. On Saturdays and Sundays, a bicycle reservation ($5) is required because space is limited.

questions.stem: What is being advertised?

options.A: A travel pass for regional trains
options.B: A guided cycling tour of the coast
options.C: A membership at a maritime museum
options.D: A boat tour of Linmouth harbor

questions.explanation: Why: The advertisement describes the Explorer Pass for “unlimited travel on all regional trains”; the museum and boat tours are only extra benefits.

questions.stem: What benefit comes with the pass?
questions.explanation: Why: Pass holders get “free entry to the Averly Maritime Museum”; boat tours are discounted by 15 percent, not free.

questions.stem: What is indicated about bicycles?

options.A: They can be rented at staffed stations.
options.B: They are not allowed on trains to Kestwick.
options.C: They are included in the 7-day pass only.
options.D: They require a paid reservation on weekends.

questions.explanation: Why: On Saturdays and Sundays “a bicycle reservation ($5) is required”; staffed stations sell passes, not bicycle rentals.

docs.text:
Yusuf Demirci 9:02 A.M.: Morning, everyone. Brisa Coffee just moved our campaign presentation up to this Thursday instead of next Monday.
Anneliese Kraus 9:04 A.M.: Thursday? The video ads won’t be finished until Friday at the earliest.
Yusuf Demirci 9:05 A.M.: I know. We could show them the storyboards and a rough cut of the first ad instead.
Tanvir Hossain 9:06 A.M.: I can have a rough cut ready by Wednesday afternoon, but only if Anneliese sends me the voice-over recordings today.
Anneliese Kraus 9:08 A.M.: Consider it done. They’ll be in the shared folder by noon.
Marisol Ybarra 9:10 A.M.: What about the print materials? Should I still order the sample posters from the printer?
Yusuf Demirci 9:11 A.M.: Yes, but ask for express delivery. We’ll need them by Wednesday.
Marisol Ybarra 9:12 A.M.: The express fee is $80. Is that within our budget?
Yusuf Demirci 9:14 A.M.: That’s fine. I’ll also ask them to book the large meeting room at their headquarters. They’re inviting their regional managers.
Marisol Ybarra 9:15 A.M.: Great. I’ll get the order in right away.

questions.stem: Why did Mr. Demirci start the discussion?

options.A: To report that a meeting date has changed
options.B: To ask for help booking a room
options.C: To announce that a client has canceled a project
options.D: To request an increase in the budget

questions.explanation: Why: He says the client “moved our campaign presentation up to this Thursday instead of next Monday”; he books a room later, but that is not why he began the chat.

questions.stem: What problem does Ms. Kraus mention?

options.A: Some voice-over recordings have been lost.
options.B: Some work will not be ready by the new date.
options.C: A printer has raised its express delivery fee.
options.D: A client has rejected the storyboards.

questions.explanation: Why: She points out that "the video ads won't be finished until Friday at the earliest," after the new Thursday date. The $80 express fee is mentioned later by Ms. Ybarra and is not a price rise, and the recordings are not lost.

questions.stem: At 9:08 A.M., what does Ms. Kraus mean when she writes, “Consider it done”?

options.A: She has finished editing the video ads.
options.B: She will send some files to Mr. Hossain.
options.C: She agrees to give the presentation.
options.D: She has already reserved a meeting room.

questions.explanation: Why: She is replying to Mr. Hossain’s condition that she send the voice-over recordings today, and adds that they will be in the shared folder by noon; the ads themselves are not finished.

questions.stem: What will Ms. Ybarra most likely do next?

options.D: Place an order with express delivery

questions.explanation: Why: After Mr. Demirci approves the $80 express fee, she says, “I’ll get the order in right away”; Mr. Demirci, not she, will arrange the meeting room.

docs.title: SunVessa P300 Portable Power Station — Getting Started
docs.text:
Thank you for purchasing the SunVessa P300. This portable battery can power laptops, small appliances, and camping lights for up to 12 hours on a single charge.
[1]
Charging: Before first use, charge the unit fully. It can be charged from a standard wall outlet (about 6 hours), a car’s 12-volt socket (about 9 hours), or the SunVessa folding solar panel, sold separately (about 8 hours in direct sunlight).
[2]
The display on the front shows the remaining battery level as a percentage.
Use: Press and hold the power button for three seconds to turn the unit on. Do not connect devices that require more than 300 watts, such as hair dryers or electric kettles.
[3]
If the unit is overloaded, it will shut off automatically to protect the battery.
Storage: When not in use, store the P300 in a cool, dry place and recharge it at least once every three months.
[4]
Your P300 is covered by a two-year warranty when registered at www.sunvessa.com within 30 days of purchase.

questions.stem: What is the P300 designed to do?
questions.explanation: Why: The instructions say it “can power laptops, small appliances, and camping lights”; it should not be used with electric kettles, and a car socket is only a way to charge it.

questions.stem: What is NOT mentioned as a way to charge the P300?
questions.explanation: Why: The unit can be charged from a wall outlet, a car's 12-volt socket or the folding solar panel. Laptops are mentioned only as devices the P300 can power, not as a way to charge it.

questions.stem: What is indicated about the solar panel?

options.A: It charges the unit faster than a wall outlet.
options.B: It is covered by a five-year warranty.
options.C: It must be registered within 30 days.
options.D: It is not included with the P300.

questions.explanation: Why: The panel is “sold separately”; it takes about 8 hours compared with 6 hours from a wall outlet, so it is slower, and the 30-day registration applies to the P300 warranty.

questions.stem: In which of the positions marked [1] , [2] , [3] , and [4] does the following sentence best belong? “The power rating of most devices can be found on a label on the device itself or on its adapter.”
questions.explanation: Why: The sentence tells users how to check whether a device exceeds the 300-watt limit, so it belongs right after that warning at [3]; the other positions discuss charging time, the display or storage.

docs.text:
Dear Reservations Team,
I am writing on behalf of Meridia Journeys to request rooms for a tour group visiting Porto from 12 to 15 May. The group consists of 22 travelers and one tour guide, so we would need 11 double rooms and one single room for three nights.
Our travelers will spend their days on excursions to the Douro Valley and will therefore need breakfast only. However, we would like to hold a private welcome dinner for the whole group on the evening of our arrival. Could you tell me whether your restaurant can accommodate a group of this size, and send me a sample set menu?
Finally, several of our travelers have difficulty with stairs, so rooms on lower floors or near an elevator would be greatly appreciated.
I look forward to your reply.
Best regards,
Oriane Vasseur
Tour Coordinator, Meridia Journeys

Dear Ms. Vasseur,
Thank you for considering Hotel Miradouro. I am happy to confirm that we can offer 11 double rooms and one single room for the nights of 12, 13, and 14 May. Our group rate is €118 per night for each double room and €92 per night for the single room, breakfast included.
Unfortunately, our restaurant has been booked for a private event on the evening of 12 May. It is, however, available the following evening, and our chef has prepared a three-course set menu at €34 per person, which I have attached. If you would prefer to keep your original date, I would be glad to recommend some nearby restaurants that welcome groups.
The double rooms we are holding for your group are all on the second and third floors, close to the elevators.
To secure the booking, please return the signed group contract by 20 March. A deposit of 20 percent of the total will then be charged to your company’s account.
Kind regards,
Henrique Valadares
Group Sales Manager, Hotel Miradouro

questions.stem: Why did Ms. Vasseur write the first e-mail?

options.A: To book a tour of the Douro Valley
options.B: To request accommodations for a group
options.C: To complain about a previous stay
options.D: To apply for a position as a tour guide

questions.explanation: Why: She writes “to request rooms for a tour group visiting Porto”; the Douro Valley excursions are already part of the travelers’ plans, not something she is booking with the hotel.

questions.stem: What is indicated about the travelers?

options.A: They will each stay in a single room.
options.B: They will spend their days elsewhere.
options.C: They will stay in Porto for a week.
options.D: They want lunch served at the hotel.

questions.explanation: Why: Ms. Vasseur says they “will spend their days on excursions to the Douro Valley” and need breakfast only; only the guide needs a single room.

questions.stem: When will the group most likely have dinner at the hotel restaurant?
questions.explanation: Why: The group arrives on 12 May, but the second e-mail says the restaurant is booked that evening and available “the following evening”, which is 13 May.

questions.stem: In the second e-mail, the word “secure” in paragraph 4, line 1, is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Why: “To secure the booking” means to make the booking certain or guaranteed; “fasten” and “protect” are other meanings of “secure” that do not fit a reservation.

questions.stem: How has Mr. Valadares responded to one of Ms. Vasseur’s requests?

options.A: By offering a discount on the single room
options.C: By placing most of the group near the elevators
options.D: By providing a free welcome dinner

questions.explanation: Why: Ms. Vasseur asked for rooms near an elevator because some travelers have difficulty with stairs, and Mr. Valadares says the double rooms are “close to the elevators”; a deposit is still required and the dinner costs €34 per person.

docs.title: Corvanta Business Connect — Plans for Growing Businesses
docs.text:
Keep your team connected with Corvanta’s new business plans. Every plan includes unlimited calls within the country, free installation, and 24-hour technical support.
Whether you run a small café or a busy office, Corvanta has a plan that grows with you. Our fiber network now reaches more than 90 percent of businesses in the metropolitan area, and our customers have rated us the region’s top business provider three years in a row.

Hello,
I own a travel agency with offices in two neighborhoods of the city. We currently have fourteen employees, each of whom needs a mobile line, and we are hiring two more agents in September. Our current provider’s internet connection is too slow for the video calls we hold with our hotel partners, so we need a speed of at least 500 Mbps.
We have been with our current provider for six years, and apart from the internet speed, we have been fairly satisfied with the service. However, our contract ends on 31 August, and I would like the new service to be running at both offices before then.
I am interested in the plan that would give everyone a line without our having to pay for additional ones. Before I sign, I would like to know whether the half-price offer still applies if installation cannot be completed until August, since our second office will not open until then. Also, could someone visit our main office to explain the plan to my business partner, who handles our finances? We are both available most weekday mornings.
Regards,
Ximena Alcántara
Owner, Alcántara Travel

questions.stem: What is NOT mentioned as a feature of all Corvanta business plans?
questions.explanation: Why: The advertisement says every plan includes unlimited calls within the country, free installation and 24-hour support; an account manager is offered only on plans with 10 or more lines.

questions.stem: Why is Ms. Alcántara dissatisfied with her current provider?

options.B: Its technical support is closed at night.
options.C: Its internet connection is too slow.
options.D: It charges extra for mobile lines.

questions.explanation: Why: She says her current provider’s “internet connection is too slow for the video calls” she holds; extra charges for lines are mentioned in Corvanta’s advertisement, not as a complaint.

questions.stem: Which plan will Ms. Alcántara most likely choose?
questions.explanation: Why: She will need 16 lines (14 employees plus 2 new agents) and at least 500 Mbps; only Premier includes more than 10 lines, so Advanced would require paying for extra lines.

questions.stem: What does Ms. Alcántara ask about?

options.A: Whether extra lines cost less in August
options.B: Whether she can end her contract early
options.C: Whether a promotional price will still apply
options.D: Whether Corvanta has a store near her office

questions.explanation: Why: She asks “whether the half-price offer still applies if installation cannot be completed until August”; August is mentioned only because of the installation date.

questions.stem: What is suggested about Alcántara Travel?

options.A: It opened its second office last year.
options.B: It will get a personal account manager.
options.C: It holds video calls with airline partners.
options.D: It has used Corvanta’s services for years.

questions.explanation: Why: The agency needs the Premier plan with 20 lines, and the advertisement says plans "with 10 or more mobile lines also include a dedicated account manager." Its second office opens in August, its video calls are with hotel partners, and it has been with another provider for six years.

docs.title: Gatherwell Event Rentals — Customer Satisfaction Policy
docs.text:
Gatherwell Event Rentals is committed to making every event a success. If you are not satisfied with any part of our service, please contact our billing department at billing@gatherwellrentals.com. The following terms apply to all rental orders.
Late delivery: If a delivery arrives more than 60 minutes after the end of the scheduled delivery window, the delivery and pickup fee will be refunded in full.
Damaged or unusable items: Customers will receive a full refund of the rental cost of any item reported as damaged or unusable within 48 hours of delivery. Photographs of the items must be provided.
Cancellations: Orders canceled at least seven days before the event date will receive a full refund of the deposit. For cancellations made after that point, the deposit will not be returned.
All refunds are issued to the original method of payment within ten business days.

docs.title: Notice to All Tenants — Brookmere Business Centre
docs.text:
Electric vehicle charging stations are being installed in the underground car park. The work will take place from Monday, 3 March, to Friday, 14 March. During this period, Level P2 will be closed.
Tenants who normally park on Level P2 may use the Ashgrove Street public car park at no charge. Please collect a free parking voucher from the reception desk on the ground floor before parking there.
When the work is complete, sixteen new charging points will be available on Level P2 to all tenants. Charging will cost $0.30 per kilowatt-hour, billed monthly to each tenant company. To register a vehicle for charging access, please contact our facilities manager, Gustavo Pellegrini, at gpellegrini@brookmerebc.com.
Contractors will work between 7:00 A.M. and 6:00 P.M., and some noise may be heard on the ground floor. We apologize for any inconvenience and thank you for your patience.

Dear Mr. Pellegrini,
Three employees at Brightwave Telecom Solutions (Suite 410) drive electric cars and would like to register for charging access once the new stations open. I have attached their names and vehicle details. At the moment, they charge their cars at home, but charging at work would be much more convenient for them.
Could you also tell me whether charging points can be reserved in advance? Our sales representatives often return to the office in the afternoon with low batteries and would like to be sure a point is free.
Finally, one of our technicians, Wiremu, usually parks on Level P2, but he was unable to collect a voucher yesterday because the reception desk was closed when he arrived at 7:30 A.M. Is there another way for him to obtain one?
Many thanks,
Aroha Tipene
Office Manager

Aroha Tipene 8:41 A.M.: Wiremu, Mr. Pellegrini replied. Reception will open at 7:00 A.M. until the construction is finished, so you can pick up a voucher tomorrow morning.
Wiremu Harlan 8:43 A.M.: Great, thanks. I’ve had to pay for parking on Ashgrove Street for the last two days. Can I get that money back?
Aroha Tipene 8:45 A.M.: Yes. He said to send your receipts to him directly and the building management will reimburse you.
Wiremu Harlan 8:46 A.M.: Perfect. Did he say anything about reserving charging points?
Aroha Tipene 8:48 A.M.: That won’t be possible, unfortunately. But he thinks sixteen points will be more than enough for the building.
Wiremu Harlan 8:50 A.M.: Good to know. I’ll drop off my receipts at his office at lunchtime.
Aroha Tipene 8:51 A.M.: Sounds good. And don’t forget to pick up your voucher tomorrow!
