directions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given below each sentence. Select the best answer to complete the sentence. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

questions.stem: The factory’s new packaging line was installed ahead of schedule; _____ , production costs fell by nearly 8 percent in the first month.
questions.explanation: Why: The fall in costs is a result of the early installation, so “consequently” is correct; “nevertheless” would wrongly signal a contrast between two positive facts.

questions.stem: _____ rising fuel prices, Vandermeer Logistics has raised its delivery charges for the first time in four years.
questions.explanation: Why: Rising fuel prices are the reason for the higher charges, so “Due to” fits; “In spite of” would illogically present the price rise as an obstacle to raising charges.

questions.stem: Several _____ customers wrote to the store manager after the weekend sale ended earlier than advertised.
questions.explanation: Why: Customers who feel an emotion are described with the -ed participle, so “disappointed” is correct; “disappointing” would describe the thing that causes the feeling, such as the sale.

questions.stem: The walking tour includes a stop at the old harbor, _____ visitors can sample fresh seafood from local vendors.
questions.explanation: Why: The clause after the gap is complete and describes a place (the harbor), so the relative adverb “where” is needed; “which” would require a missing subject or object in the clause.

questions.stem: The new staff scheduling software was _____ adopted by all twelve of the chain’s restaurants within a month.
questions.explanation: Why: An adverb is needed to modify the passive verb “was adopted”, so “successfully” is correct; “successful” is an adjective and cannot modify a verb.

questions.stem: Please keep your original receipt, as it is required for any _____ or exchange of merchandise.
questions.explanation: Why: A receipt is needed to return goods for a “refund or exchange”, which is the standard collocation; a “discount” or “deposit” is not something a customer obtains by returning merchandise.

questions.stem: Ms. Albescu prefers to review the quarterly sales figures _____ before presenting them to the board of directors.
questions.explanation: Why: The reflexive pronoun “herself” is used for emphasis to mean that Ms. Albescu does the review personally; “her” and “hers” cannot stand alone after the object here.

questions.stem: By the time the new assembly plant opens next spring, the company _____ more than 300 additional workers.
questions.explanation: Why: “By the time … opens next spring” refers to an action completed before a future point, so the future perfect “will have hired” is required; “had hired” refers to the past.

questions.stem: The _____ of the new visitor center has been postponed until the city approves the revised building plans.
questions.explanation: Why: After “The” and before “of”, a noun is required, so “construction” is correct; the other choices are a verb, an adjective and a participle.

questions.stem: _____ employee attending the safety seminar at the pharmaceutical plant must sign in at the front desk.
questions.explanation: Why: The singular noun “employee” and singular verb pattern require “Every”; “All”, “Most” and “Many” must be followed by a plural noun such as “employees”.

questions.stem: The Riverside Farmers Market is open every Saturday _____ 7:00 A.M. until noon from May through October.
questions.explanation: Why: “From … until …” marks the start and end of a period, so “from” is correct; “since” is used with a past starting point and a perfect tense.

questions.stem: Each of the rental cars at our airport locations _____ inspected for damage before it is released to a customer.
questions.explanation: Why: The subject is “Each”, which is singular, so “is” is required; “are” is the trap that agrees with the nearby plural noun “cars”.

questions.stem: Visitors to the Kestrel Pharmaceuticals research laboratory must _____ a valid photo ID at the security desk.
questions.explanation: Why: One “presents” identification when asked to show it, so “present” fits; “express”, “perform” and “attend” do not collocate with “a photo ID”.

questions.stem: The new staff fitness room is located directly _____ the main lobby, on the second floor of the building.
questions.explanation: Why: The fitness room is on the floor over the lobby, so “above” is correct; “between” would need two reference points and “among” needs a group.

questions.stem: The company’s new return policy aims to _____ the time required to process customer refunds.
questions.explanation: Why: After “aims to”, a base-form verb that can take the object “the time” is required, so “shorten” is correct; the other choices are an adjective, an adverb and a noun.

questions.stem: Mr. Vaillancourt will lead the factory tour _____ Ms. Oyelaran is attending the trade fair in Frankfurt.
questions.explanation: Why: A conjunction is needed before the clause “Ms. Oyelaran is attending …”, and “while” shows the two events happen at the same time; “during” and “despite” are prepositions and cannot introduce a clause.

questions.stem: Customers have praised the new line of kitchen appliances for its _____ design and low energy use.
questions.explanation: Why: An adjective is needed to describe the noun “design”, so “attractive” is correct; “attractively” is an adverb and “attract” is a verb.

questions.stem: The travel agency recommends _____ hotel reservations at least two months in advance during the festival season.
questions.explanation: Why: “Recommend” is followed by a gerund when there is no personal object, so “making” is correct; “recommends to make” is a common learner error.

questions.stem: _____ its popular morning news program, Channel 9 will also begin broadcasting a weekly business show in March.
questions.explanation: Why: The word “also” shows the business show will be added to the news program, so “In addition to” is correct; “As long as” is a conjunction and cannot come before a noun phrase.

questions.stem: Tickets for the Lakeshore Food Festival are expected to sell out quickly, so early booking is _____ recommended.
questions.explanation: Why: “Highly recommended” is the fixed collocation meaning strongly advised; “deeply”, “tightly” and “heavily” do not combine with “recommended”.

questions.stem: Applicants for the parts manager position should have a _____ knowledge of automotive parts and accessories.
questions.explanation: Why: “A thorough knowledge” means a complete and detailed knowledge, which is the natural collocation; “lengthy” describes duration and “generous” describes amounts or people.

questions.stem: Orders placed through our website are _____ ready for pickup within two hours of confirmation.
questions.explanation: Why: “Typically” (= usually) fits a general statement about how soon orders are ready. “Briefly” describes duration (ready briefly?), and “evenly” and “mutually” do not collocate with “ready for pickup.”

questions.stem: Ms. Khoury _____ as head chef at the Marigold Bistro ever since it first opened in 2019.
questions.explanation: Why: “Ever since it first opened in 2019” describes a situation continuing up to now, so the present perfect “has worked” is required. Trap: “had worked” (past perfect) needs a later past reference point, which the sentence does not have.

questions.stem: If the shipment of spare parts _____ by Friday, the repair work on the delivery trucks would begin on Monday.
questions.explanation: Why: The main clause uses “would begin”, so the if-clause needs the simple past “arrived” (second conditional); “had arrived” would require “would have begun”.

questions.stem: All returned merchandise is _____ inspected before it is placed back on the store shelves.
questions.explanation: Why: “Thoroughly inspected” (= checked carefully and completely) is the natural collocation. “Highly” goes with adjectives like “recommended,” “greatly” with verbs of change like “improved,” and “widely” with “used” or “known.”

questions.stem: The hotel’s rooftop restaurant will close for renovations in July; _____ , guests may enjoy breakfast in the lobby café.
questions.explanation: Why: The café is offered during the period of the closure, so “in the meantime” is correct; “otherwise” would mean “if the restaurant does not close”, which is illogical.

questions.stem: The Alderton plant produced _____ more vehicles last quarter than any other factory in the region.
questions.explanation: Why: A comparative (“more … than”) is intensified with “considerably,” “much,” or “far.” Trap: “very more” is a common learner error — “very” cannot modify a comparative; “such” and “so” do not work before “more” here.

questions.stem: Staff members who wish to attend the training workshop should submit their registration forms _____ Wednesday, 4 March.
questions.explanation: Why: A deadline for a one-time action (“submit”) takes “by.” Trap: “until” is used for a continuing state (“The office is open until Wednesday”); “within” needs a period of time, and “since” needs a perfect tense.

questions.stem: The festival organizers decided to move the concert indoors _____ forecasts of heavy rain for the weekend.
questions.explanation: Why: The gap is followed by a noun phrase (“forecasts of heavy rain”), so a preposition is needed; “in light of” (= because of) gives the reason. “Even though,” “provided that” and “so that” are conjunctions and must be followed by a clause.

questions.stem: The results of the customer satisfaction survey will be _____ to all department heads once the analysis is complete.
questions.explanation: Why: Results (things) are “distributed to” people. Trap: “informed” and “notified” take a person as their object (“department heads will be informed of the results”), so “the results will be informed” is wrong; “acquainted” also needs a person.

directions: Read the texts that follow. A word, phrase, or sentence is missing in parts of each text. Four answer choices for each question are given below the text. Select the best answer to complete the text. Then mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

docs.title: Attention, Brightfield Mall Tenants and Staff
docs.text:
The north parking garage will be closed for resurfacing from Monday, 14 April, through Sunday, 27 April. During this period, all store employees
131
to park in the overflow lot on Carver Street. Customer parking in the south garage will not be affected.
A free shuttle bus will run between the Carver Street lot and the mall’s east entrance every ten minutes
132
7:00 A.M. and 10:00 P.M. Staff who work later than 10:00 P.M. may request a security escort to their vehicles by calling the front desk.
We understand that this
133
may cause some inconvenience, particularly during the busy Easter weekend.
134
Please direct any questions to the mall management office at extension 220.
Thank you for your cooperation.
Brightfield Mall Management

questions.explanation: Why: The employees receive the request, so the passive “are asked” is needed; “have asked” is active and would mean the employees made the request.
Why: The pattern “between 7:00 A.M. and 10:00 P.M.” is completed by “and”, so “between” is correct; “from” would need “to” or “until”.
Why: “This” refers back to the closing of the north garage described in the first paragraph, so “closure” is correct; nothing in the notice mentions a promotion or a delivery.

options.A: The work is necessary, however, to keep the garage safe for everyone.
options.B: As a result, the south garage will be reserved for staff during this time.
options.C: We are pleased to report that the resurfacing work has now been completed.
options.D: For this reason, the Easter weekend sale has been postponed until May.

questions.explanation: Why: After admitting the closure “may cause some inconvenience,” the notice justifies it — “however” signals that contrast. B contradicts the first paragraph (staff must use the Carver Street lot; the south garage is for customers), C has the wrong time (the work has not started), and D is never supported by the notice.

docs.title: Kerrow Valley Farm — Guided Farm Tours
docs.text:
Every weekend from June to September, Kerrow Valley Farm opens its gates to visitors
135
want to see how their food is grown. Our two-hour guided tour takes you through the apple orchards, the dairy barn, and our new greenhouse, where we grow tomatoes and herbs all year round.
Our guides, all of whom live and work on the farm, give
136
explanations of each stage of production, from planting to packing. Children can help feed the calves, and everyone is invited to taste fresh milk and cheese made on site.
At the end of the tour, guests are welcome to pick their own strawberries in the fields behind the farmhouse.
137
Tickets cost $18 for adults and $9 for children under twelve. Because group sizes are limited to 20 people, we
138
booking online at least a week before your visit. Tours depart at 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M. from the farm shop.

questions.explanation: Why: The relative pronoun refers to people (visitors) and acts as the subject of “want”, so “who” is correct; “which” is used for things.
Why: An adjective is needed before the noun “explanations”, so the participle adjective “detailed” is correct; “detail” and “details” are nouns.

options.A: Visitors are asked not to touch any of the animals during the tour.
options.B: Baskets are provided, and the fruit is sold by weight at the farm shop.
options.C: The greenhouse part of the tour is offered only to school groups.
options.D: Strawberries are usually in season on the farm from April to May.

questions.explanation: Why: The sentence continues the idea of picking strawberries by explaining how the fruit is collected and paid for. A contradicts “children can help feed the calves,” C contradicts the tour that goes “through… our new greenhouse,” and D clashes with tours that run from June to September and end with strawberry picking.

Why: The web page gives current general information in the present tense (“Tickets cost”, “Tours depart”), so the simple present “advise” is correct; the past forms do not fit an ongoing recommendation.

docs.title: Is Your Car Ready for Winter?
docs.text:
Cold weather is hard on vehicles. That is why Halvorsen Auto Care is offering a complete winter inspection throughout November. Book before 30 November and pay just $39, a
139
of 40 percent off our regular price.
Our certified technicians will check your battery, tires, brakes, lights, and heating system, and they will top up your windshield washer fluid with a winter formula. The inspection takes
140
45 minutes, so there is no need to leave your car with us. Simply relax in our comfortable customer lounge.
141
Customers who have the inspection done will also receive a coupon for 15 percent off any repairs
142
during the inspection. The coupon is valid until 31 January.
To book, call 555-0176 or visit any of our three locations in Eastfield, Morton, and Barrow Hill.

questions.explanation: Why: After the article “a” and before “of”, a noun is required, so “reduction” is correct; “reduce” is a verb and “reduced” is a participle.
Why: “About” is used before a number to mean approximately, so “takes about 45 minutes” is correct; “much”, “very” and “quite” cannot modify a number in this way.

options.A: Our technicians will call you when the car is ready to collect the next day.
options.B: Please note that the lounge is currently closed for renovation.
options.C: A courtesy car can be provided while your vehicle is with us.
options.D: Free coffee and Wi-Fi are available while you wait.

questions.explanation: Why: The sentence continues the idea of relaxing in the lounge while the 45-minute inspection is done. A and C assume the car stays at the garage, which contradicts “there is no need to leave your car with us,” and B contradicts the invitation to “relax in our comfortable customer lounge.”
Why: The repairs are found by the technicians, so the reduced passive “identified” (= that are identified) is correct; “identifying” would mean the repairs do the identifying.

docs.title: Installing Your ShelfLink Digital Price Labels
docs.text:
Before you begin, make sure that the ShelfLink base station is plugged in and
143
to your store’s wireless network. The small light on the front of the station will turn blue when it is ready.
Next, attach each label to the front edge of the shelf using the adhesive strip on the back. Press
144
for about ten seconds so that the label stays in place. Labels should be placed at least five centimeters apart.
The labels will display prices automatically once they are linked to your inventory system.
145
, you will need to scan the barcode on each label with the ShelfLink app on your tablet or smartphone. The app will confirm each successful link with a green check mark.
146
Once all labels are linked, any price change you make in your inventory system will appear on the shelves within two minutes.

questions.explanation: Why: The gap is joined by “and” to the participle “plugged in”, so the parallel past participle “connected” is required.
Why: An adverb is needed to describe how to press, so “firmly” is correct; “firm” and “firmer” are adjectives.
Why: The sentence explains how the labels are linked to the inventory system mentioned in the previous sentence, so “To do this” is correct; “In contrast” and “Even so” wrongly signal opposition.

options.A: The light on the base station will then turn blue.
options.B: If a red cross appears instead, repeat the scan from a closer distance.
options.C: Each label must then be removed and attached to the shelf again.
options.D: Prices can then be changed by hand on each label.

questions.explanation: Why: After the green check mark for a successful link, the instructions logically explain what to do if the link fails. A belongs to the first step (setting up the base station), C contradicts pressing the label firmly so it “stays in place,” and D contradicts prices that appear “automatically.”

directions: In this part you will read a selection of texts, such as magazine and newspaper articles, e-mails, and instant messages. Each text or set of texts is followed by several questions. Select the best answer for each question and mark the letter (A), (B), (C), or (D) on your answer sheet.

docs.text:
Lorenzo Batista 9:12 A.M.: Hi Priya. The produce delivery just came, but Greenfield Farms sent only half the tomatoes we ordered.
Priya Ramanathan 9:14 A.M.: Again? That’s the second time this month.
Lorenzo Batista 9:15 A.M.: We need at least ten kilos for today’s lunch specials.
Priya Ramanathan 9:17 A.M.: I’ll call them and ask for the rest to be sent before 11:00. If they can’t manage it, I’ll pick some up at the wholesale market on my way in.
Lorenzo Batista 9:18 A.M.: Sounds good. Should I take the tomato soup off the menu board for now?
Priya Ramanathan 9:19 A.M.: Let’s hold off on that.
Lorenzo Batista 9:20 A.M.: OK. I’ll start preparing the other dishes, then.

questions.stem: What problem does Mr. Batista report?
questions.explanation: Why: Mr. Batista says the supplier “sent only half the tomatoes we ordered”, so the order was incomplete; nothing suggests the delivery was late or the produce was spoiled.

questions.stem: At 9:19 A.M., what does Ms. Ramanathan most likely mean when she writes, “Let’s hold off on that”?

options.A: She wants to add a new lunch special.
options.B: She will update the menu board herself.
options.C: She believes the soup can still be served.
options.D: She thinks the delivery should be refused.

questions.explanation: Why: She plans to get the missing tomatoes before lunch, so she tells Mr. Batista not to remove the tomato soup yet; she does not offer to change the board herself.

docs.title: Dunmore Fleet Services — Vehicle Maintenance Request
docs.text:
Description of problem: The check-engine light came on while I was driving to a client’s office yesterday, and the van has been making a grinding noise whenever I brake. I need the van for a sales trip to Portsmouth on 10 March, so I would appreciate it if the work could be completed before then. If the repairs will take longer, please arrange a replacement vehicle for the trip.
FOR OFFICE USE ONLY — Assigned to: T. Villanueva | Estimated completion: 7 March | Replacement vehicle needed: No

questions.stem: Why was the form submitted?

options.A: To reserve a van for a sales trip
options.B: To request repairs to a vehicle

questions.explanation: Why: Mr. Asante describes a warning light and a grinding noise and asks for the work to be done; the sales trip is mentioned only as the reason for his deadline.

questions.stem: What is indicated about the van?

options.A: It is expected to be ready before the sales trip.
options.B: It will be replaced with a new vehicle.
options.C: It was dropped off on 3 March.
options.D: It has been driven more than 50,000 km.

questions.explanation: Why: The estimated completion date is 7 March, before the 10 March trip, and the office marked that no replacement is needed; 3 March is the date the form was submitted.

docs.title: Notice to Passengers — Winter Timetable
docs.text:
Beginning 1 October, the Port Aldous–Merrow Island ferry will operate on its winter timetable. Departures from Port Aldous will be reduced from eight to five per day, with the first sailing at 7:30 A.M. and the last at 6:00 P.M. The café on the upper deck will be open on weekends only.
Because the vessel used in winter carries only 24 cars, passengers traveling with vehicles are strongly encouraged to reserve space in advance. Reservations can be made at www.aldousferries.com or at the ticket office in either port. Foot passengers and cyclists do not need a reservation.
Monthly commuter passes purchased before 1 October will remain valid until their expiration date. The summer timetable will return on 1 April.
Aldous Island Ferries

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the notice?

options.A: To announce a new ferry route
options.B: To advertise a café on a ferry
options.C: To explain an increase in fares
options.D: To inform passengers about changes to a service

questions.explanation: Why: The notice describes the winter timetable, with fewer departures and reduced café hours; it does not mention a new route or higher fares.

questions.stem: What are passengers with cars advised to do?

options.A: Book a place ahead of time

questions.explanation: Why: The notice says drivers are “strongly encouraged to reserve space in advance”; commuter passes and the upper deck are mentioned for other reasons.

docs.title: Harborview Suites — Guest Satisfaction Survey
docs.text: Comments: The front desk staff were wonderful. Mr. Adeyemi even arranged a late checkout so that I could return to my room between my final client meeting and my flight home. My only real disappointment was breakfast. By 8:30 most of the hot dishes had run out and were not replaced, which was frustrating when I had early appointments to get to. I will be back in the area in September for a conference and would consider staying here again if this situation improves.

questions.stem: What is indicated about Ms. Solberg?

options.A: She stayed at the hotel for a week.
options.C: She used the fitness center every day.

questions.explanation: Why: She mentions client meetings, early appointments and a conference, which show she was on a business trip; her stay lasted from 12 to 15 May, not a week.

questions.stem: What does Ms. Solberg want the hotel to improve?

options.A: The supply of food in the morning
options.B: The speed of the check-in process
options.D: The hours of the fitness center

questions.explanation: Why: She complains that the hot breakfast dishes ran out and were not replaced; she gave check-in the highest rating.

docs.title: Northbeam Radio 94.7 — Share Your Story on Community Voices
docs.text:
Every Sunday at 10:00 A.M., Northbeam Radio airs Community Voices, a half-hour program featuring true stories from listeners across the Tallis Bay region. We are especially interested in stories about local businesses, volunteers, and neighborhood traditions.
How to submit: Send us a written summary of no more than 300 words using the form below, and include a telephone number so that one of our producers can contact you. Because we receive hundreds of submissions each month, we are able to reply only to those people whose stories are selected for the program.
Selected contributors are invited to our studio on Dace Street to record their story with a producer. Recording sessions usually last about an hour. Contributors who are unable to travel to the studio can record at home using a free recording kit, which we will send to them by mail.
As a thank-you, every contributor receives a Northbeam Radio travel mug and a digital copy of the finished broadcast.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the web page?

options.A: To announce the launch of a radio station
options.B: To advertise a recording studio for rent
options.C: To invite listeners to send in stories
options.D: To recruit volunteers to produce a program

questions.explanation: Why: The page explains how listeners can submit stories for Community Voices; the studio is mentioned only as the place where selected stories are recorded.

questions.stem: What is stated about submissions?

options.A: They must be recorded at home.
options.B: They should be longer than 300 words.
options.C: They are accepted only by telephone.
options.D: Not all of them will receive a response.

questions.explanation: Why: The station replies “only to those people whose stories are selected”, so many submissions get no answer; summaries must be no more than 300 words and are sent through a form.

questions.stem: What will contributors who cannot visit the studio receive?

options.C: A call from the program host

questions.explanation: Why: Those who cannot travel get “a free recording kit, which we will send to them by mail”; “travel” appears only in “travel mug”, which every contributor receives.

docs.title: GreenRoot Liquid Plant Food — For vegetables, flowers, and houseplants
docs.text:
Net contents: 1 liter (makes up to 200 liters of plant food solution)
Directions: Shake well before use. Mix one capful (5 ml) with 1 liter of water. For outdoor plants, apply every two weeks during the growing season (March to September). For houseplants, apply once a month throughout the year. Do not apply to dry soil; water plants lightly before feeding.
Storage: Keep the bottle tightly closed in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Do not allow the product to freeze. Keep out of reach of children and pets.
Made by Talvera Agricultural Products, Fresno, California. Questions? Call our gardening helpline at 1-800-555-0192, Monday to Friday, 8:00 A.M. to 5:00 P.M., or visit talvera-agri.com for seasonal planting tips.

questions.stem: How often should the product be used on indoor plants?
questions.explanation: Why: The label says to feed houseplants “once a month throughout the year”; every two weeks applies to outdoor plants in the growing season.

questions.stem: What are users instructed to do before applying the product?

options.C: Measure the temperature of the soil

questions.explanation: Why: The directions say “water plants lightly before feeding” because the product should not go on dry soil; sunlight is mentioned only in the storage instructions.

questions.stem: What is indicated on the label?

options.A: Advice is available by telephone on weekdays.
options.B: The product should be kept in a freezer.
options.C: One bottle makes 1 liter of solution.
options.D: The product is suitable only for vegetables.

questions.explanation: Why: A gardening helpline is open Monday to Friday; the label says the product must not freeze and that one bottle makes up to 200 liters.

docs.title: Dining Out: Saffron & Salt, 42 Kellerman Avenue
docs.text:
When chef Nadia Farouk closed her small lunch counter at the Eastgate Market last year, many of her regular customers feared they had eaten the last of her spiced lamb flatbreads. They need not have worried. Ms. Farouk has reopened in a much larger space on Kellerman Avenue, and the flatbreads are still on the menu, along with an expanded choice of dinner dishes inspired by her travels in Morocco and Turkey.
I visited on a busy Friday evening. Although every table was taken, our server was attentive and our food arrived promptly. The grilled vegetable platter was generous enough for two people, but the slow-cooked chicken with apricots was the highlight of the meal. My only complaint concerns the desserts, which were rather ordinary compared with everything else.
Prices are reasonable, with all main courses priced between $16 and $24. Saffron & Salt is open Tuesday through Sunday from 5:00 P.M. to 10:00 P.M. Reservations are recommended on weekends.

questions.stem: What is suggested about Ms. Farouk?

options.A: She used to run a smaller food business.
options.C: She writes reviews for a newspaper.
options.D: She still works at the Eastgate Market.

questions.explanation: Why: The review says she “closed her small lunch counter at the Eastgate Market”, so she previously ran a smaller business; she no longer works at the market.

questions.stem: What did the reviewer enjoy most?
questions.explanation: Why: He calls the slow-cooked chicken with apricots “the highlight of the meal”; the vegetable platter is described only as generous, and the desserts were ordinary.

questions.stem: What is NOT indicated about Saffron & Salt?

options.C: Its main courses cost less than $25.
options.D: It can be crowded on Friday evenings.

questions.explanation: Why: The restaurant opens at 5:00 P.M., so it does not serve lunch; being open Tuesday through Sunday, prices up to $24 and the busy Friday visit are all stated.

docs.text:
Hyun-woo Baek 2:05 P.M.: Quick update: Line 3 is down again. The labeling machine keeps jamming.
Adaeze Nwosu 2:06 P.M.: How long will it take to fix?
Hyun-woo Baek 2:07 P.M.: The technician says at least three hours. He has to get a replacement roller from the supplier.
Adaeze Nwosu 2:08 P.M.: That’s a problem. The Merriton order is supposed to go out first thing tomorrow — 4,000 bottles of pasta sauce.
Gustavo Pereira 2:10 P.M.: Line 1 finishes its current run at 3:30. We could move the Merriton job over there.
Adaeze Nwosu 2:11 P.M.: Would that delay anything else?
Gustavo Pereira 2:12 P.M.: The Holloway order would slip to Thursday, but they don’t need it until next week anyway.
Adaeze Nwosu 2:13 P.M.: Then let’s go with that. Mei, could you let the warehouse know the pallets will be ready later than planned?
Mei Rautio 2:15 P.M.: Sure. I’ll message them now, and I’ll ask the evening shift to stay until all the bottles are packed.
Hyun-woo Baek 2:16 P.M.: Thanks, everyone. I’ll post again once Line 3 is running.

questions.stem: What problem is being discussed?

options.A: A supplier sent the wrong labels.
options.B: A machine is not working properly.
options.C: A shipment was damaged in transit.

questions.explanation: Why: Mr. Baek reports that “the labeling machine keeps jamming”; the technician is available but needs a part from the supplier.

questions.stem: What is suggested about the Merriton order?

options.A: It has been canceled by the customer.
options.B: It will be produced on Line 3.
options.C: It is scheduled to be shipped the next day.
options.D: It is smaller than the Holloway order.

questions.explanation: Why: Ms. Nwosu says the order “is supposed to go out first thing tomorrow”; it will be moved to Line 1, not Line 3.

questions.stem: At 2:13 P.M., what does Ms. Nwosu mean when she writes, “Then let’s go with that”?

options.A: She wants the Holloway order shipped first.
options.B: She will contact the supplier herself.
options.C: She agrees to wait for the repair.

questions.explanation: Why: After learning that moving the job to Line 1 would only delay an order that is not urgent, she accepts Mr. Pereira’s plan; she does not choose to wait for Line 3 to be repaired.

questions.stem: What will Ms. Rautio most likely do next?

options.D: Notify the warehouse of a delay

questions.explanation: Why: Asked to tell the warehouse that the pallets will be late, she replies “I’ll message them now”; the roller is being obtained by the technician.

docs.text:
As you know, construction of the new laboratory building on the west side of the Lindgate Pharmaceuticals campus is now complete. I am pleased to announce that the Research and Development department will begin moving into the building on Monday, 8 September.
[1]
The move will take place in stages over three weeks so that ongoing experiments are disrupted as little as possible.
The analytical chemistry team will move first, followed by the formulation team during the week of 15 September. The quality control laboratory will remain in its current location until the end of the month, as its new testing equipment has not yet been delivered.
[2]
Each team leader will receive a detailed moving schedule by 29 August. In the meantime, please begin labeling your equipment and supplies using the colored stickers available from the facilities office.
[3]
Items without a label may not be delivered to the correct room.
Please note that staff will not be able to enter the new building until their security badges have been updated.
[4]
Badges can be updated at the reception desk in the main building on any weekday between 9:00 A.M. and 4:00 P.M. If you have questions about the move, please contact me at extension 4417.

options.A: To provide information about a relocation
options.B: To describe a new research project
options.C: To introduce a new facilities manager
options.D: To request help with a construction project

questions.explanation: Why: The memo explains when and how the department will move into the new laboratory building; the construction is already complete.

options.A: It will be the first to move.
options.B: It is already on the west side of the campus.
options.C: It is waiting for equipment to arrive.

questions.explanation: Why: It will stay where it is because “its new testing equipment has not yet been delivered”; the analytical chemistry team moves first.

options.C: Stop by the reception desk in the main building
options.D: Collect keys from their team leader

questions.explanation: Why: Staff cannot enter “until their security badges have been updated,” and badges “can be updated at the reception desk in the main building.” Trap: team leaders receive a moving schedule; staff do not submit one.

docs.title: Castellan Motors Announces New Battery Plant in Rennick
docs.text:
DETROIT, 4 June — Castellan Motors today announced plans to build a battery manufacturing plant in Rennick, Ohio, the company’s first facility dedicated to producing batteries for electric vehicles.
[1]
Construction will begin in October, and the plant is expected to start operating in early 2028.
The 60,000-square-meter facility will supply batteries for Castellan’s popular Vireo compact SUV as well as two new models that the company plans to introduce over the next three years.
[2]
Once it reaches full capacity, the plant will employ approximately 1,200 people.
“Rennick offered everything we were looking for: an experienced workforce, excellent rail connections, and strong support from the local government,” said Castellan CEO Martin Oduya.
[3]
The company is also working with Rennick Community College to develop a training program for future employees. Classes in battery assembly and quality testing will be offered free of charge starting next spring.
[4]
More information about job openings will be posted on the Castellan Motors careers page in the coming months.

questions.stem: What is the press release mainly about?

options.A: The launch of a new vehicle model
options.B: The construction of a new production facility
options.C: The appointment of a company executive
options.D: The opening of a community college

questions.explanation: Why: The release announces a new battery manufacturing plant; new models and the college are mentioned only as related details.

questions.stem: According to the press release, what will happen in October?

options.C: A new SUV will be introduced.

questions.explanation: Why: “Construction will begin in October”; production starts in 2028 and classes start next spring.

questions.stem: What is NOT mentioned as a reason for choosing Rennick?
questions.explanation: Why: Mr. Oduya mentions an experienced workforce, rail connections and local government support, but not the cost of construction.

questions.stem: In which of the positions marked [1] , [2] , [3] , and [4] does the following sentence best belong? “Participants who complete the program will be guaranteed an interview for a position at the plant.”
questions.explanation: Why: “The program” refers to the training program with free classes described just before position [4], and the next sentence about job openings continues the topic.

docs.title: Brennan Cooking School — October Evening and Weekend Workshops
docs.text:
All ingredients, aprons, and equipment are provided, and participants take home everything they make. Each workshop is limited to 12 participants.
Participants who cancel at least 72 hours before a workshop receive a full refund. Later cancellations are not refunded, but the registration may be transferred to another workshop for a $10 fee. Students enrolled in the school’s Professional Chef program receive a 20 percent discount on all workshops.
Registration opens two weeks before each workshop and can be completed online at www.brennancooking.com or at our front desk. Gift certificates are available in any amount.

Hello,
I am registered for the pasta workshop this Saturday morning, but I have just been asked to work that day and will not be able to attend. I realize it is too late for a refund, but I would like to transfer to the same workshop later in the month, if any places are still available. I understand there is a small charge for this, and I am happy to pay it.
Also, my husband would like to join me for a class. He is a keen baker and was hoping to take the bread workshop, but he works late on Wednesdays. Will that workshop be offered again on a weekend in November? If so, we would both like to sign up for it.
By the way, I took the knife skills class last month and enjoyed it very much. Mr. Achebe was an excellent teacher, and I have been recommending your school to all my friends.
Thank you for your help.
Delphine Moreau

options.D: To apply for a teaching position

questions.explanation: Why: She wants “the same workshop later in the month”, and the schedule shows Fresh Pasta Basics again on 18 October; 4 October is the class she will miss.

options.B: The maximum size of a class
options.C: The equipment used in a class
options.D: A future date for a class

docs.text:
Dear Mr. Quintero,
Thank you for the prompt shipment of our spring order, which arrived at our warehouse yesterday. Unfortunately, when our staff unpacked the boxes, they found that 18 of the 60 blue serving bowls were chipped or cracked. The damage seems to have been caused by a lack of packing material, as the bowls had been stacked directly on top of one another.
We would prefer replacements rather than a refund, since the bowls are featured in our summer catalog, which will be mailed to customers on 20 May. Could you let me know whether you can ship replacements before that date? I have attached photographs of the damaged items for your records. Our warehouse team has set the damaged bowls aside until we hear from you.
In addition, our stores in Brampton and Lisle have reported strong sales of your olive-green coffee mugs. I would like to add 120 of them to our next regular order in June.
Best regards,
Oksana Petrenko
Senior Buyer, Hollin & Crane Home Goods

Dear Ms. Petrenko,
I am very sorry about the condition of the bowls, and thank you for sending the photographs. We have already addressed the matter with our packing team, and your future orders will be packed with extra protective material.
We have 12 blue serving bowls in stock, and I will send them to you by express courier today at no charge. The remaining six will come from our next production run and should reach you by 16 May. Please do not return the damaged bowls; you may dispose of them or keep them for display purposes. Our shipping department will e-mail you the tracking number for today’s courier delivery this afternoon.
I am delighted to hear that the olive-green mugs are selling well. Once again, please accept our apologies. As a thank-you for your patience, I will apply a 10 percent discount to the mugs in your June order.
Sincerely,
Rafael Quintero
Customer Accounts, Marlowe Ceramics

questions.stem: Why did Ms. Petrenko write to Mr. Quintero?

options.A: To place her company’s first order
options.B: To report a problem with a shipment
options.C: To request a copy of a catalog
options.D: To cancel part of an order

questions.explanation: Why: She writes that 18 of the bowls arrived chipped or cracked; she asks for replacements rather than cancelling anything.

questions.stem: What does Ms. Petrenko indicate about the serving bowls?

options.C: They are available in olive green.
options.D: They appear in an upcoming publication.

questions.explanation: Why: The bowls are “featured in our summer catalog, which will be mailed … on 20 May”; the strong sales in Brampton refer to the olive-green mugs.

questions.stem: In the second e-mail, the word “addressed” in paragraph 1, line 2, is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Why: “We have already addressed the matter with our packing team” means the problem has been dealt with; “mailed” reflects the meaning of addressing a letter, which does not fit here.

questions.stem: What is suggested about the replacement bowls?

options.A: They will be sent from a store in Brampton.
options.B: Hollin & Crane will have to pay for them.
options.C: All of them should arrive before the catalog is mailed.
options.D: Some of them are no longer being produced.

questions.explanation: Why: Twelve bowls are sent today and the last six should arrive by 16 May (second e-mail), which is before the catalog mailing on 20 May (first e-mail).

questions.stem: What does Mr. Quintero offer to do?

options.A: Pay for express shipping on all future orders
options.B: Reduce the price of some items
options.C: Refund the cost of the damaged bowls
options.D: Collect the damaged bowls from the warehouse

questions.explanation: Why: He will “apply a 10 percent discount to the mugs in your June order”; he tells her not to return the damaged bowls, and she did not want a refund.

docs.title: Kettleby Coffee Roasters — Wholesale Program for Cafés and Restaurants
docs.text:
Kettleby has been roasting small-batch coffee in Wellmont since 2009. We buy our beans directly from growers in Colombia, Ethiopia, and Guatemala, and our buyers visit each partner farm at least once a year. Every bag is roasted to order, never taken from old stock. Our wholesale customers enjoy:
• Freshly roasted beans, shipped within 48 hours of roasting
• Free delivery on orders over $300 within the Wellmont area
• A free barista training session for new wholesale customers (for up to four staff members)
• Volume pricing: 5% off orders of 20–39 kg and 10% off orders of 40 kg or more
All beans are sold in 1 kg bags. Not sure which blend is right for your business? New customers can request a free sample pack of any three blends by calling 555-0148.
About our training: Sessions last three hours and take place at our roastery on Denholm Street. Our head barista covers grinding, espresso extraction, and milk steaming. Additional staff members beyond the first four may join for $25 per person.

docs.title: Kettleby Coffee Roasters — Wholesale Order Form
docs.text: Special instructions: Please deliver before 7:00 A.M., as we open at 7:30. Our delivery entrance is at the side of the building on Pell Street. We would also like to arrange the training session for our staff.

Hello,
Our first order arrived at 6:45 on Friday morning, well before we opened, which we really appreciated. The coffee has already been very popular with our customers, especially the espresso. Several customers have even asked whether they can buy bags of beans to brew at home. However, one item was short: we received only 10 of the House Blend bags we ordered. Could you please send the rest as soon as possible, ideally with an early-morning delivery like the first one? We are almost out.
Regarding the training session, five of our baristas would like to attend. I understand that there is normally a limit, so I would be willing to pay for the additional person if necessary. Any weekday afternoon next week would suit us, as the café is quieter after 2:00 P.M. and I can manage without them for a few hours.
Finally, we are thinking of adding a decaffeinated coffee to our menu. Is there any way we could try your decaf blend before ordering it?
Best regards,
Yusuf Demir
Owner, The Linden Tree Café

questions.explanation: Why: The advertisement lists training, free delivery over $300 and free samples, and its discounts depend on order size, not on paying early.

options.B: It is located outside the Wellmont area.

questions.explanation: Why: The order form shows 15 kg (bags) of House Blend, and Mr. Demir received only 10, so 5 are missing; 15 is the full quantity ordered.

options.D: He is not a new wholesale customer.

docs.title: Tour Coordinator — Solano Heritage Tours, Lisbon
docs.text:
Solano Heritage Tours, which offers walking and coach tours of Portugal’s historic towns, is seeking a full-time Tour Coordinator to plan itineraries, manage bookings, and support our team of guides. The coordinator will also respond to customer inquiries by phone and e-mail and help train new guides each spring.
Requirements: at least two years of experience in the tourism industry; fluency in English and Portuguese; a valid driver’s license. Knowledge of a third language, especially Spanish or French, is strongly preferred. The successful candidate should be available to start on 1 September.
To apply, send a CV and cover letter to Marta Figueiredo at hr@solanotours.pt by 30 June. Interviews will be held during the week of 7 July at our office on Rua das Flores. Candidates living outside Lisbon may request a video interview.
We offer a competitive salary, 25 days of paid vacation, and free tours for employees’ family members.

Dear Ms. Figueiredo,
Please find attached my CV and cover letter for the Tour Coordinator position advertised on your Web site. For the past three years, I have worked as a guide for a cycling tour company in Porto, leading groups of up to fifteen visitors. Spanish is my first language, and I am also fluent in English and Portuguese. In my current role, I also manage the company’s online booking system and respond to customer reviews, which I believe has prepared me well for the planning side of the position.
Although I live in Porto, I would prefer to travel to Lisbon for an interview so that I can meet your team in person. However, I will be leading a tour group in the Douro Valley from 7 to 9 July. I would therefore be grateful if my interview could be scheduled for later that week.
I have also attached a reference letter from my current employer, Rota Verde Cycling Tours. Thank you for considering my application.
Sincerely,
Nicolás Iturbe

docs.title: Solano Heritage Tours — Tour Coordinator Interviews
docs.text: Note: Tiago Mendes will be at the International Tourism Fair in Madrid on 11 July. Ana Ribeiro (Senior Guide) will take his place on the interview panel that day. Each interview will last about 45 minutes. Candidates attending in person should report to the reception desk on the second floor.

options.D: He would like a video interview.

questions.explanation: Why: The posting strongly prefers a third language such as Spanish, and Mr. Iturbe’s first language is Spanish; he lives in Porto and wants to meet in person.

docs.text:
As many of you know, Horizon Travel will launch a digital edition of the magazine in January. In addition to all the articles from the print edition, it will offer short videos, interactive maps, and a searchable archive of past issues. To prepare for the launch, I have scheduled a planning meeting for Thursday, 11 September, from 9:30 A.M. to noon in Conference Room B. Attendance is required for all section editors (News, Features, Culture, and City Guides) and members of the marketing team; other staff are welcome to attend.
Before the meeting, please read the draft project plan, which I have uploaded to the shared drive. If you would like to add an item to the agenda, send it to my assistant, Kofi Mensah, by Friday, 5 September. The final agenda will be distributed on Monday, 8 September. Staff who are unable to attend will receive a summary of the discussion the following week.
Lunch will be served in the staff lounge after the meeting for everyone who attends.

docs.title: Horizon Travel — Digital Edition Planning Meeting
docs.text: Please bring a laptop or tablet to view the app prototype. Coffee and pastries will be available during the break.

Hi Beatriz,
I’ve just learned that the photographer I hired for our Iceland feature can meet only on Thursday morning, because she flies to Reykjavik that afternoon. The Iceland story will be the cover feature of our February issue, so it’s important that everything goes smoothly. Since the shoot is scheduled for October, I really need to go over the details with her before she leaves. Would it be possible for me to swap slots with Carla? That way I could meet the photographer at 10:30 and still be back in plenty of time. I’ve already checked with Carla, and she doesn’t mind. Please let me know if the change works for you.
Also, I’ve read the project plan on the shared drive. The section on video assumes that each editor will film his or her own content, but most of us have no filming experience at all. I’d like to propose hiring a freelance video producer for the first six months, and I’ll include cost estimates in my presentation.
Thanks,
Emeka
